Events.RelatedBody: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in Aspire. This advisory provides guidance on updating affected applications and components. Aspire Dashboard's unauthenticated NotFound route can permit telemetry deletion in both standalone and AppHost-hosted deployments. In standalone deployments using browser-token authentication, it can also expose the browser token. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/microsoft/aspire/issues/22148 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** Critical - **Score:** 9.1 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N` - **Weakness:** CWE-862 ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Any supported OS - **Architectures:** x64, Arm64 ## Affected Packages ### Standalone Aspire Dashboard Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- Aspire Dashboard | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 Both 13.6.3 and 13.6.4 contain the unauthenticated NotFound route. ### Aspire Dashboard SDK packages Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.linux-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.linux-x64) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.linux-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.linux-arm64) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.linux-musl-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.linux-musl-x64) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.osx-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.osx-x64) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.osx-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.osx-arm64) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.win-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.win-x64) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.win-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.win-arm64) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? Aspire Dashboard releases through 13.6.4 are affected, whether deployed independently or launched by an Aspire AppHost. For an AppHost using Dashboard SDK packages, check the resolved Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk package versions against the affected ranges above. If the AppHost selects a CLI-bundled Dashboard or a custom Dashboard path, check the version of that Dashboard instead. Aspire ships independently of .NET; installing a .NET runtime or SDK update does not replace the Dashboard. ### How do I fix the issue? Update Aspire Dashboard to version 13.6.5 or later. Neither 13.6.3 nor 13.6.4 is a fixed upgrade target. For container deployments, explicitly set the Dashboard image to `mcr.microsoft.com/aspire/dashboard:13.6.5` and recreate or redeploy the container. Replace older version tags and nightly image references, including those in generated Docker Compose or Kubernetes manifests, with this fixed stable image. Updating AppHost package references alone does not replace an image reference in an existing deployment manifest. For an AppHost using Dashboard SDK packages, update any explicit Aspire.Hosting.AppHost version, including a central package version, to 13.6.5 or later. If that reference is supplied implicitly by Aspire.AppHost.Sdk, update the SDK reference to 13.6.5 or later instead. Restore and rebuild the AppHost, verify that its resolved Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk packages are 13.6.5 or later, and restart the AppHost to run the updated Dashboard. If your AppHost selects a CLI-bundled Dashboard or a custom Dashboard path, update the Dashboard in that selected bundle or location to 13.6.5 or later and restart the AppHost. Updating AppHost package references alone does not replace that Dashboard. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Further information can be found in the MSRC [Report an Issue FAQ](https://www.microsoft.com/msrc/faqs-report-an-issue). Security reports made through MSRC may qualify for the Microsoft .NET Bounty. Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue in the Aspire repository at https://github.com/microsoft/aspire. The Announcements repo (https://github.com/dotnet/Announcements) will contain this bulletin as an issue and will include a link to a discussion issue. You can ask questions in the linked discussion issue. ### Disclaimer The information provided in this advisory is provided "as is" without warranty of any kind. Microsoft disclaims all warranties, either express or implied, including the warranties of merchantability and fitness for a particular purpose. In no event shall Microsoft Corporation or its suppliers be liable for any damages whatsoever including direct, indirect, incidental, consequential, loss of business profits or special damages, even if Microsoft Corporation or its suppliers have been advised of the possibility of such damages. Some states do not allow the exclusion or limitation of liability for consequential or incidental damages so the foregoing limitation may not apply. ### External Links [CVE-2026-118740](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-118740) ### Acknowledgements - Weeraphat Srisutham ### Revisions V1.0 (November 10, 2026): Advisory published.

## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in ASP.NET Core. This advisory provides guidance on updating affected applications and components. ASP.NET Core Identity scaffolding templates use the request-supplied email instead of the account's stored email for password-reset and confirmation messages. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/Scaffolding/issues/3959 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 8.1 (base score) - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H/E:U/RL:O/RC:C` - **Weakness:** CWE-640 ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Any supported OS - **Architectures:** All ## Affected Packages Updating scaffolding packages/tools does not repair previously generated application code. Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc contains the affected templates. Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design is a parent package that brings in the MVC generator through a minimum-version dependency. For Design, applicability depends on the resolved MVC generator: a project that independently resolves a fixed MVC version does not become vulnerable merely because it retains an older Design reference. ### 8.0 - standalone packages Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc) | >= 8.0.0, <= 8.0.23 | 8.0.24 [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design) | >= 8.0.0, <= 8.0.23 | 8.0.24 ### 9.0 - standalone packages Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc) | >= 9.0.0, <= 9.0.12 | 9.0.13 [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design) | >= 9.0.0, <= 9.0.12 | 9.0.13 ### 10.0 - standalone packages Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc) | >= 10.0.0, <= 10.0.2 | 10.0.3 [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design) | >= 10.0.0, <= 10.0.2 | 10.0.3 ### Additional known affected scaffolding prereleases These are exact known affected versions, not continuous prerelease intervals. Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold 20.3.0 Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold-aspnet has been incorporated into Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold. Version 20.3.0 supports .NET 8, 9, 10 and 11. Install it as a .NET tool, not as a project package reference. The MVC and Design project packages use the separate fixed versions listed above; 20.3.0 is not a version of those packages. ### Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold 20.x Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold) | >= 20.0.0-preview.1.26156.3, <= 20.1.0 | 20.3.0 The 20.x tool contains the vulnerable Identity and Blazor templates for .NET 8.0 through 11.0. ### Affected legacy prereleases The following exact versions also contain affected templates: - [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc) and [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design): `11.0.0-preview.1.26156.3` and `11.0.0-preview.1.26230.3`. - [Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold-aspnet](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold-aspnet): `10.0.0-rc.1.25458.5` and `10.0.0-rc.1.25468.1`. Apply the generated-code repair below to applications created with these versions. For new scaffolding, use the Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold 20.3.0 tool, which supports .NET 8 through 11. Migrating to that tool is not an update to an MVC or Design project package reference and does not repair previously generated code. ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? Check both the installed scaffolding package/tool version and the code it generated. Applications generated with an affected template remain affected after the tool is updated unless their handlers are corrected. The `dotnet-aspnet-codegenerator` command loads generators from the application's dependencies. Check the project's Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design and Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc references against the versions above; updating only the command-line tool does not replace those project dependencies. For applications created with `dotnet new`, check the selected SDK with `dotnet --version` in the working directory. ### Describe the bug

Running `dotnet publish /t:PublishContainer` on a project that targets `net481` fails, even when `ContainerBaseImage` is set explicitly. The `ComputeDotnetBaseImageAndTag` task throws because it gets a four-part version (`4.8.1.0`) that `NuGet.Versioning.SemanticVersion.Parse` can't read.

The failure happens while the task logs telemetry. Base-image inference isn't involved, since the user already supplied the image.

### To Reproduce

1. A project with `<TargetFramework>net481</TargetFramework>` and `<OutputType>Exe</OutputType>`.
2. Run:
   ```
   dotnet publish -c Release -r win-x64 --self-contained /t:PublishContainer ^
     -p:ContainerBaseImage=mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/framework/runtime:4.8.1-windowsservercore-ltsc2022 ^
     -p:ContainerRepository=myapp ^
     -p:ContainerArchiveOutputPath=out/image.tar.gz
   ```

### Expected behavior

Since `ContainerBaseImage` is set, the task should return it unchanged and the container should be built.

### Actual behavior

```
Microsoft.NET.Build.Containers.targets(53,5): error MSB4018: The "ComputeDotnetBaseImageAndTag" task failed unexpectedly.
System.ArgumentException: '4.8.1.0' is not a valid version string. (Parameter 'value')
   at NuGet.Versioning.SemanticVersion.Parse(String value)
   at Microsoft.NET.Build.Containers.Tasks.ComputeDotnetBaseImageAndTag.ParseSemVerToMajorMinor(String semver) in ComputeDotnetBaseImageAndTag.cs:line 345
   at Microsoft.NET.Build.Containers.Tasks.ComputeDotnetBaseImageAndTag.LogNoInferencePerformedTelemetry() in ComputeDotnetBaseImageAndTag.cs:line 331
   at Microsoft.NET.Build.Containers.Tasks.ComputeDotnetBaseImageAndTag.Execute() in ComputeDotnetBaseImageAndTag.cs:line 103
```

### Root cause

In `Microsoft.NET.Build.Containers.targets`, the `ComputeContainerBaseImage` target passes:

```xml
<ComputeDotnetBaseImageAndTag
    UserBaseImage="$(ContainerBaseImage)"
    TargetFrameworkVersion="$(_TargetFrameworkVersionWithoutV).0"
    ... />
```

Appending `.0` assumes `_TargetFrameworkVersionWithoutV` always has two parts:

| TFM | `_TargetFrameworkVersionWithoutV` | Passed value | `SemanticVersion.Parse` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `net8.0` | `8.0` | `8.0.0` | OK |
| `net48` | `4.8` | `4.8.0` | OK |
| `net481` | `4.8.1` | `4.8.1.0` | **throws** |
| `net462` / `net472` | `4.6.2` / `4.7.2` | `4.6.2.0` / `4.7.2.0` | **throws** |

In `ComputeDotnetBaseImageAndTag.cs`:

- `Execute()` calls `LogNoInferencePerformedTelemetry()` when `UserBaseImage` is set.
- That method calls `ParseSemVerToMajorMinor(TargetFrameworkVersion)`, which uses the strict `SemanticVersion.Parse(semver)`.
- The exception escapes `Execute()`, so publishing fails with MSB4018. Collecting telemetry shouldn't be able to fail a build.

`ComputeVersionPart()` uses `SemanticVersion.TryParse` instead, so the inference path handles this case. Only the telemetry paths (`LogNoInferencePerformedTelemetry` and `LogInferencePerformedTelemetry`) use the throwing `Parse`.

### Suggested fix (any of these)

1. In the targets, pass the version without blindly adding `.0`. For example, normalize it with `$([System.Version]::Parse(...))`, or only append `.0` when the value has two parts.
2. In `ParseSemVerToMajorMinor`, use `NuGet.Versioning.NuGetVersion.TryParse`, which accepts four-part versions, or `System.Version.TryParse`. Fall back to the raw string or `null` when parsing fails.
3. Wrap telemetry collection in a try/catch so it can never fail the build.

### Workaround

Add these targets to the project (or `Directory.Build.targets`). They temporarily shorten `_TargetFrameworkVersionWithoutV` to `major.minor` for the container base-image computation, then restore it:

```xml
<!-- SDK container targets pass "$(_TargetFrameworkVersionWithoutV).0" to a strict SemVer parser;
     "4.8.1.0" (net481) fails, so expose a 2-part version only for that task. -->
<Target Name="_FixNetFxVersionForContainerBaseImage"
        BeforeTargets="ComputeContainerBaseImage"
        Condition="'$(TargetFrameworkIdentifier)' == '.NETFramework'">
  <PropertyGroup>
    <_OriginalTargetFrameworkVersionWithoutV>$(_TargetFrameworkVersionWithoutV)</_OriginalTargetFrameworkVersionWithoutV>
    <_TargetFrameworkVersionWithoutV>$([System.Version]::Parse('$(_TargetFrameworkVersionWithoutV)').ToString(2))</_TargetFrameworkVersionWithoutV>
  </PropertyGroup>
</Target>

<Target Name="_RestoreNetFxVersionAfterContainerBaseImage"
        AfterTargets="ComputeContainerBaseImage"
        Condition="'$(_OriginalTargetFrameworkVersionWithoutV)' != ''">
  <PropertyGroup>
    <_TargetFrameworkVersionWithoutV>$(_OriginalTargetFrameworkVersionWithoutV)</_TargetFrameworkVersionWithoutV>
  </PropertyGroup>
</Target>
```

With this, the task receives `4.8.0`, which parses, and the user-supplied `ContainerBaseImage` is passed through unchanged.

- Target framework: `net481`, RID `win-x64`, self-contained

Issues.Title: [release/3.1] Reset current_no_gc_region_info after leaving no gc region implicitly
Issues.Body:
Backport https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/73602.

## Customer Impact
Customers reported occasional `System.InvalidOperationException` with message `The NoGCRegion mode was already in progress` when calling `GC.TryStartNoGCRegion`. This is preventing them from using this optimization and impacting their cold start latencies.

## Testing
Customers have tried the fix on .NET 6 overnight and reported the exception never appears again. Meanwhile, there is an unpatched machine and observed 72 exceptions of the same type in the same time interval, proving this does fix the bug.

## Risk
Low. This only impact customer using `TryStartNoGCRegion`, and this is the right thing to do.

Issues.Title: Migrate FabricBot Tasks to Config-as-Code
Issues.Body:
**TL;DR;** Requesting to add [FabricBot](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/fabricbot_overview) configuration associated with your repository to `.github/fabricbot.json`.

**Context**

FabricBot is now a [config-as-code-only](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/bot-config-as-code) platform. As a result, while you can still use the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/coreclr) to modify your FabricBot configuration, you can no longer save the changes. The only way to save changes to your configuration at the moment is to _export configuration_ from the portal and upload the exported configuration to `.github/fabricbot.json` in your repository. In this pull request, we are adding your FabricBot configuration to your repository at `.github/fabricbot.json` so that you can make changes to it going forward.

While the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/coreclr) is the *only way* to modify your FabricBot configuration at the moment, we have a feature on our backlog to publish the JSON schema defining the structure of the FabricBot configuration file. With the JSON schema, you can (1) use a plaintext editor of your choice to modify the FabricBot configuration file and use the schema to validate the file after editing or (2) [configure](https://code.visualstudio.com/Docs/languages/json#_json-schemas-and-settings) VS Code to use the schema when editing FabricBot configuration file to take advantage of convenience features such as automatic code completion and field description on mouseover.

[*Pull Request Create*](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/prcreate), a [MerlinBot](https://https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot) Extension, was used to automatically create this pull request. If you have any questions or concerns with this pull request, please contact [MerlinBot Expert DRI](mailto:merlinbotdri@microsoft.com).

Issues.Title: Questions about tagging within this repository / future versions
Issues.Body:
I was looking through this repository to determine if .NET Standard 2.1 libraries support default interface methods - it looks like they do, given the presence of `System.Runtime.CompilerServices.RuntimeFeature.DefaultImplementationsOfInterfaces`, as well as my own experimenting in VS 2019. It seems I was mistaken when thinking that this was not the case, so I'm glad this repository is easily accessible to determine this.

But while doing this, I found it difficult to determine what commits were included in this particular .NET Standard version. I see that there's a tag `v2.1.0-prerelease.19126.1`, as well as branches `release/2.0.0`, `release/3.0`, and `release/3.0-preview9`. One of the machines I tested VS 2019 on had a `netstandard.dll` assembly, itself targeting .NETStandard v2.1.0, with AssemblyInformationalVersion `1.1.0+a5b5f2e1e369972c8ff1e2183979fab6099f52ef`; this commit is part of the `release/3.0` branch. However, another machine had a same-named assembly, targeting .NETCoreApp v3.0 and AssemblyInformationalVersion `3.0.0+4ac4c0367003fe3973a3648eb0715ddb0e3bbcea`, and I don't see that commit hash in this repository.

Additionally, [this blog post](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/dotnet/the-future-of-net-standard/) states that 2.1 will be the last version, but there is another prerelease tag `v2.2.0-prerelease.19564.1` and [on GitHub](https://github.com/dotnet/standard/releases/tag/v2.2.0-prerelease.19564.1) it's labelled .NET 5.0 Preview 2.

So I have a few questions for understanding this repository:

1. Since .NET Standard 2.1 is released, are there plans to continue development in this repository for e.g. the shared BCL going forward with .NET 5+?
2. Are there multiple kinds of `netstandard.dll` for a single .NET Standard version? E.g. are there separate versions for .NET Framework to reference and for .NET Core / .NET 5+ to reference?
3. Do the tags / branch names in this repository correspond to a .NET Standard version or something else?
4. It looks like there are patch releases; are there patch versions of a single .NET Standard version?
5. Are there other repositories which are being used to create `netstandard.dll`?
6. Is there a way to determine, from the repository, which commit is the one used for a given release?

Thank you for your consideration.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Questions about tagging within this repository / future versions" (#1777)

Issues.Title: Issue with resolving between .NET Standard 2.0 and .NET Standard 2.1
Issues.Body:
# Summary

.NET Standard version is not resolved correctly when a transitive dependency targets multiple .NET Standard versions.

# Environment

- Windows 10 (19042.746)
- .NET 5 SDK 5.0.201

# Minimal reproducible example
[bug.zip](https://github.com/dotnet/standard/files/6209239/bug.zip)

This is a three-project solution:
- `TestProject1` targeting `netcoreapp3.1`
- `ClassProject1` targeting `netstandard2.0`
- `ClassProject2` targeting *both* `netstandard2.0` and `netstandard2.1`

The project dependency chain is: `TestProject1 -> ClassProject1 -> ClassProject2`

A method (`ClassProject2Test1`) on `ClassProject2` is hidden behind a `#if NETSTANDARD2_0` preprocessor directive.

# The issue

The unit test failed with a `MissingMethodException`

```
[xUnit.net 00:00:00.38]     TestProject1.UnitTest1.Test1 [FAIL]
  Failed TestProject1.UnitTest1.Test1 [2 ms]
  Error Message:
   System.MissingMethodException : Method not found: 'Void ClassLibrary2.Class2.Class2Test1()'.
  Stack Trace:
     at ClassLibrary1.Class1.Class1Test1()
   at TestProject1.UnitTest1.Test1() in C:\Users\rex\source\netstandard-bug-repro\TestProject1\UnitTest1.cs:line 12
```

# Expected result

The compiler should have resolved the chain as:

`TestProject1 (.NET Core 3.1) -> ClassProject1 (.NET Standard 2.0) -> *ClassProject2 (.NET Standard 2.0)*` 

# Actual result

The compiler resolved the chain as:

`TestProject1 (.NET Core 3.1) -> ClassProject1 (.NET Standard 2.0) -> *ClassProject2 (.NET Standard 2.1)*` 

Which causes the exception because the offending method, `ClassProject2Test1`, was hidden by the `#if NETSTANDARD2_0` preprocessor directive.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Issue with resolving between .NET Standard 2.0 and .NET Standard 2.1" (#1787)

Issues.Title: Security Vulnerability due to System.Text.RegularExpressions
Issues.Body:
### Problem
There is a security vulnerability with the version of System.Text.RegularExpressions that is used by dotnet standard. The vulnerable version of System.Text.RegularExpressions is 4.3.0. Please see links below for the vulnerability documentation or discussion:

https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/en-US/vulnerability/CVE-2019-0820
https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/111
https://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2019-0820
https://snyk.io/vuln/SNYK-DOTNET-SYSTEMTEXTREGULAREXPRESSIONS-174708
https://www.whitesourcesoftware.com/vulnerability-database/CVE-2019-0820

The dotnet commit that fixed the vulnerability is https://github.com/dotnet/corefx/commit/19d4b1163d8a03dd90ff5fd1785eea6305112545

### Issue:
We use whitesource and it has caught this issue with high severity. We don't consume System.Text.RegularExpressions directly but packages that use this. Therefore as a transitive dependency due to NetStandard library, which is being used by several other dotnet packages like Castle Windsor, MassTransit etc., Once an update is available the others could followup and update.

### Code:

[The latest version 2.0.3 of Net standard ](https://www.nuget.org/packages/NETStandard.Library/) still seem to be using System.Text.RegularExpressions version 4.3.0 as per https://github.com/dotnet/standard/blob/master/src/apicompat/netstandard/netstandard.depproj

### Fix
Please update[ library](https://www.nuget.org/packages/NETStandard.Library/) targeting .netStandard 1.6 to update System.Text.RegularExpression package to latest secured version 4.3.1 to fix the security issue or kindly suggest alternatives.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Security Vulnerability due to System.Text.RegularExpressions" (#1786)

Issues.Title: linq using GetValueOrDefault  in Where clause problem
Issues.Body:
Hello,

I am currently using .NET core 2.2.x and EF Core. 2.2.6. I have a function that returns a List<Animal> from the database with no issue. It returns 11 results. However, when I try to use `.Where(p => p.DeletedAt.GetValueOrDefault(DateTime.Now) => DateTime.Now).ToList()`, it still should return 11 results, however it returns 0. I also eliminated the possibility that there is something wrong with my where clause (logic) because it works perfectly on 4.6.1 EF Core 2.2.6. Furthermore, I confirmed that it is only where I am comparing a nullable type using that function and I am guessing that I missed a thread someone opened on this issue. I am aware .NET core 2.2 is not LTS. I also thought this goes here because it's not AFAIK, an EF core issue but rather an Ienumerable/Linq issue.

Update: As it turns out your notion of `DateTime.Now` getting evaluated twice is true. To rectify that, I will now be using `DateTime.Now.Date`. This is odd because this exact code works on 4.6.1. You're probably right. SMH. Thank you @GrabYourPitchforks! You may now close.

Microsoft (R) .NET Framework Strong Name Utility Version 4.0.30319.0

Issues.Title: System.Drawing.Printing.PrinterSettings slow
Issues.Body:
_This issue has been moved from [a ticket on Developer Community](https://developercommunity2.visualstudio.com/t/SystemDrawingPrintingPrinterSettings-/890524)._ --- Hello I'm debugging a problem with the printer settings. Some calls are significant slower if the default printer is a network printer, even if I explicit set a local printer name. After studying referencesource I think I found the culprit. I call: var printerSettings = new System.Drawing.Printing.PrinterSettings(); printerSettings.PrinterName = "LOCALPRINTER"; // the next call is slow if the OS default printer is a network printer var res = printerSettings.DefaultPageSettings.PrinterResolution Internally FastDeviceCapabilities is called. FastDeviceCapabilities calls GetOutputPort. But GetOutput port return the port of the default printer and not the port of the given printer! In addition, DeviceCapabilities is then called with a wrong combination of printer name and port, don't know if this could lead to additional problems. Resolution: GetOutputPort should return the port of the given printer and not accessing the default printer at all. Best Regards, Raphael --- ### Original Comments #### Raphael Affolter on 1/20/2020, 04:03 AM:

I forgot to mention: .Net Framework 4.6.1

#### Feedback Bot on 1/20/2020, 06:51 PM:

Because we print a lot, we really suffer from this performance penalty.

Also reading PaperSizes and PaperSources from the printer settings is slow caused by the same problem.

Best Regards,

Raphael

Issues.Title: Build issues when referencing project that targets multiple frameworks C# WPF
Issues.Body:
I'm working on converting a large WPF solution's projects to SDK style and ran into some issues.

The solution is large with multiple projects(old style) all targeting .net452 and some nugets(some made by me) installed, targeting both .net452 and .netstandard2.1 This all seems to work fine, somehow the nuget manages to install the correct version targeting .net452.

I have decided to slowly convert the projects inside the solution to SDK style targeting .net452 and .netstandard2.1 just like the nugets.

This is where the problem starts, one project was converted so far that is referenced by multiple other projects. Localy everything seems to build and run fine, however when Azure DevOps(VS version 2019) is used to build the solution there are 2 scenarios:

1. The famous error message is shown:

                "Error CS0012: The type 'Object' is defined in an assembly that is not referenced. You must add a reference to assembly 
                 'netstandard, Version=2.1.0.0"

2. It builds fine but on app launch it crashes with:

                 "Could not load file or assembly 'netstandard, Version=2.1.0.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=cc7b13ffcd2ddd51' 
                 or one of its dependencies. The system cannot find the file specified."

I'm suspecting that the problem is related to referencing the SDK project, it looks like that somehow it references the .netstandard2.1 instead of the .net452.

The reason this is my suspicion is that if targetframework is set to only .net452 on the referenced project everything works fine. Google has led me to two possible solutions to tell the project what framework to use from the reference:

```
<ProjectReference Include="..\..\..\..\foo\foo.csproj"
                  AdditionalProperties="TargetFramework=net452">
      <Project>{xxxxxx-xxxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxxxx}</Project>
      <Name>foo</Name>
</ProjectReference>
```
and

```
<ProjectReference Include="..\..\..\..\foo\foo.csproj">
      <SetTargetFramework>TargetFramework=net452</SetTargetFramework>
      <Project>{xxxxxx-xxxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxxxx}</Project>
      <<Name>foo</Name>
</ProjectReference>
```
This doesn't look like it's doing anything and the problem still persists. At the moment I ran out of ideas and I'm here asking for help. Please let me know what I'm doing wrong or what else I can try.

**Context**

FabricBot is now a [config-as-code-only](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/bot-config-as-code) platform. As a result, while you can still use the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/corefx) to modify your FabricBot configuration, you can no longer save the changes. The only way to save changes to your configuration at the moment is to _export configuration_ from the portal and upload the exported configuration to `.github/fabricbot.json` in your repository. While the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/corefx) is the *only way* to modify your FabricBot configuration at the moment, we have a feature on our backlog to publish the JSON schema defining the structure of the FabricBot configuration file. With the JSON schema, you can (1) use a plaintext editor of your choice to modify the FabricBot configuration file and use the schema to validate the file after editing or (2) [configure](https://code.visualstudio.com/Docs/languages/json#_json-schemas-and-settings) VS Code to use the schema when editing FabricBot configuration file to take advantage of convenience features such as automatic code completion and field description on mouseover.

Issues.Title: Fix RSA OAEP decryption in OpenSSL with non-power-of-two keys lengths
Issues.Body:
## Customer Impact

A customer reported in dotnet/runtime#71607 that decrypting RSA OAEP with SHA2 and a 3072-bit key on Linux resulted in a OAEP de-padding error, while other platforms were able to perform these operations successfully.

Investigation in to the issue led to uncover that RSA OAEP decryption that uses the managed implementation does not work with non-power-of-two keys because we do not slice a rented buffer accordingly. The current implementation only works because `CryptoPool.Rent` happens to give back power-of-two arrays which are exactly the same size as the key.

The fix is to slice the data to the correct size.

This does not affect dotnet/runtime because the managed implementation of RSA OAEP is no longer used for OpenSSL RSA decryption. This change was introduced in dotnet/runtime#50063.

## Testing

Unit tests were introduced to test RSA OAEP encryption with a 3072-bit RSA key. These tests will be forward-ported to dotnet/runtime.

## Risk

Minimal. The change is localized and understood that a `Slice` was missing.

Issues.Title: Don't re-run Razor tag helper discovery for method body edits
Issues.Body:
Analysis of https://dev.azure.com/devdiv/DevDiv/_workitems/edit/3105280 showed a couple of issues that cause delays in repeated editing of a Razor file. One is to limit UI thread usage/requests by throttling or debouncing, which is currently with the debugger team, but the trace and memory dump analysis showed that Razor was re-running tag helper discovery when even a single whitespace character is added to a method body in a Razor file. That's not ideal.

This adds a step to the source generator to only re-process syntax trees that have changes outside of a method body.

## Benchmarks

Release measurements from a synthetic workload of 300 components, 5 MVC views, 100 C# helper files with 50 methods each, and 20 tag helpers. Times are median `GeneratorDriver.RunGenerators` wall times; allocations are mean per generator run. These are temporary Stopwatch-harness results, not BenchmarkDotNet measurements or end-to-end Visual Studio timings.

| Scenario | Edits | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| C# method-body edits, same file | 40 | 88.7 ms; 7.53 MB | 10.1 ms; 0.57 MB |
| C# method-body edits, 100 different files | 100 | 73.5 ms; 7.37 MB | 9.0 ms; 0.58 MB |
| Razor `@code` body edits, same file | — | 83.2 ms; 8.27 MB | 8.0 ms; 1.40 MB |
| Razor `@code` body edits, different files | — | 82.1 ms; 8.43 MB | 8.3 ms; 1.40 MB |
| Mixed: 9 body edits followed by 1 signature edit | 60 | 73.1 ms; 7.64 MB | 3.5 ms; 1.60 MB |
| Fallback present, C# body edits in different files | 50 | 65.1 ms; 7.40 MB | 3.2 ms; 0.58 MB |
| Fallback present, Razor `@code` body edits | 30 | 68.4 ms; 8.55 MB | 7.6 ms; 1.41 MB |

Discovery ran 0 times for 100 C# body edits, 30 times for 30 signature edits, and 6 times for 60 mixed edits.

**Trade-offs:** Signature-edit medians were 119.1 ms before and 125.7 ms after in the main run. Across repeats, they were 113–119 ms before and 126–129 ms after, a roughly 6–14% regression. Initial generation was 1306 ms before and 1378 ms after by median, but the measured ranges overlapped (948–1728 ms and 1041–1734 ms), so that difference may be noise.

## Compilation retention

Counts include the input compilation held by the benchmark harness. Retained memory is the heap difference with and without the generator driver after a forced full GC.

| Scenario | Compilations before → after | Retained memory before → after |
|---|---:|---:|
| Initial run | 2 → 2 | 18.79 → 18.81 MB |
| 100 C# body edits | 3 → 3 | 23.07 → 21.58 MB |
| Body edit → signature edit → body edit | 3 → 4 | 23.55 → 23.34 MB |

The signature-edit sequence retains one additional compilation in the fast-discovery cache until discovery runs again. Compilations did not accumulate across edits in the other measured scenarios.
 ###### Microsoft Reviewers: [Open in CodeFlow](https://microsoft.github.io/open-pr/?codeflow=https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/pull/86641)

Issues.Title: Use `Get[Async]IterationType` APIs in `foreach` snippet provider
Issues.Body:
Since compiler now exposes APIs to obtain iteration type of a given type, `foreach` snippet is its primary consumer. By porting snippet availability checks to this new APIs we can now trivially offer inline/postfix `.foreach` for pattern-based enumerables, most notably `[ReadOnly]Span<T>` and `ConfiguredCancellableAsyncEnumerable<T>` (this is the result of `WithCancelllation` and `ConfigureAwait` extensions on `IAsyncEnumerable<T>`). Added tests for both. I also made postfix `foreach` obey user's `var` preferences - the snippet initially generates full type as iteration type, then the simplifier collapses it down to a `var` is configured to do so. This targets specifically postfix variants and ignores normal ones since the snippet can make the wrong guess if multiple enumerables are available in the scope and additionally fixing iteration type after inserting the snippet can become a burden rather than a helper

Issues.Title: Suppress diagnostic fixes when multiple members are selected
Issues.Body:
Similar to [#86634](https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/pull/86634), this reduces clutter when multiple members are selected. This time, we suppress code fixes such as "Make field readonly" and "Remove unused member".

Selecting several members indicates that the user wants to work with them together. For example, generating a constructor from two selected fields should produce parameters for both. Code fixes currently ignore that group and can offer a change for just one member, making the useful refactorings harder to find.

In the future, code fixes could use selections too, such as making all selected fields readonly. That behavior isn't supported today, so hiding these entries removes clutter without losing an existing capability. Fixes remain available when a single member is selected, since selecting one field is a reasonable way to request fixes for it.

Issues.Body:

Today, the list also includes actions that appear simply because the selection is inside a type, making the useful options harder to find. For example: "Move type," "Add debugger display," and "Convert to record."

This change keeps the list focused: a refactoring should appear for a member selection only when the selected members affect what it does.

Issues.Title: Trim entries and ignore empty segments when splitting TargetFrameworks
Issues.Body:
### Summary
Previously, `ProjectBuildManager` split `<TargetFrameworks>` directly with `Split(';')` without trimming surrounding whitespace or newlines, and without filtering out empty segments. For example, values like `net8.0; net10.0`, `net8.0;\r\n    net10.0`, `  net10.0\r\n  `, or trailing/consecutive semicolons such as `net8.0;net10.0;` could produce untrimmed target framework names or empty/null entries passed into MSBuild's `TargetFramework` global property during `BuildProjectInstancesAsync` (resulting in broken project loading, missing/unexpected metadata references, or `ArgumentNullException` in `SetGlobalProperty`).

### Changes
- Added `ProjectBuildManager.SplitTargetFrameworks` to split `<TargetFrameworks>` on `;`, trim each entry, and omit empty/whitespace-only entries while keeping `net472` compatibility without LINQ or modern `StringSplitOptions` allocations.
- Updated `BuildProjectInstancesAsync` to iterate over the trimmed, non-empty target framework list when setting the `TargetFramework` global property and re-evaluating projects.
- Added test coverage in `NetCoreTests` verifying projects with spaces after semicolons, surrounding whitespace/newlines, single-TFM whitespace formatting, and trailing/empty semicolons.

Fixes #86592

Issues.Title: Union creation expression requires a `CollectionBuilderAttribute` on it, but only if the collection value is specified inline and without the `new` keyword.
Issues.Body:
**Version Used**: .NET SDK 11.0.0., `<LangVersion>preview</LangVersion>`, `<Nullable>enable</Nullable>`.

For a union, one of whose variants is a collection, the compiler allows instantiation either by directly calling the union constructor, or from a ready-made collection stored in a variable. When specifying a collection variant inline, the compiler requires a `CollectionBuilderAttribute` on the union, as well as an `IEnumerable<>` implementation on the union.

**Repro**:

```csharp
IList<string> threeSides = ["Top", "Left", "Right"];

StringsVariant sides1 = threeSides;

StringsVariant sides2 = new(["Top", "Left", "Right"]);

StringsVariant sides3 = ["Top", "Left", "Right"]; // error here

readonly union StringsVariant(string, IList<string>);
```

Diagnostics:

```
Error (active)	CS9174	Cannot initialize type 'StringsVariant' with a collection expression because the type is not constructible.	Program.cs	7
```
**Expected Behavior**:

Expect to be able to use instance creation without the `new` noise or extra variable, as unions allow for for non-collection variants. There's little point in implementing a factory method for `CollectionBuilderAttribute`, much less an entire `IEnumerable<>` interface. Also expect a relaxed factory requirement for the structure with `UnionAttribute`, as well as for the variant with constructors via `IUnionMembers`.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Union creation expression requires a `CollectionBuilderAttribute` on it, but only if the collection value is specified inline and without the `new` keyword." (#86621)

Issues.Title: Handle UnresolvedAnalyzerReference when computing a project checksum
Issues.Body:
Fixes #86613

`SerializerService.CreateChecksum(AnalyzerReference)` had no case for `UnresolvedAnalyzerReference` and threw `UnexpectedValue`. `MSBuildWorkspace` creates that reference for every analyzer path that does not exist on disk, so any caller of the project checksum failed on such a project. `SymbolFinder.FindReferencesAsync` reaches it in-process for overrides, through the project index in `DependentTypeFinder`.

The checksum now covers an unresolved reference with a type marker and its path. It stays stable while the reference is unresolved and differs from an `AnalyzerFileReference` to the same path, which matches how a missing file behind an `AnalyzerFileReference` is already handled (`TryGetFileReferenceMvid` returns `Guid.Empty`). `WriteAnalyzerReferenceTo` and `ReadAnalyzerReferenceFrom` handle it too, so a solution holding one can be synced to the remote host; the find-references test runs both in process and out of process.

Issues.Title: [API Proposal]: SymbolFinder.FindReferencesAsync overload that selects the inheritance cascade
Issues.Body:
**Updates:**
- 2026-11-24: after review feedback, the options type is the existing `FindReferencesSearchOptions`, made public with the cascade mode as its only public member. The property is `CascadeMode` because the type already has an internal `bool Cascade`.

## Background and Motivation

Every public overload of `SymbolFinder.FindReferencesAsync` searches with the rename-style inheritance cascade: for a member involved in inheritance, it walks up and down the hierarchy from every symbol it finds, until nothing new turns up. For an override of a `System.Object` member, that brings in every other override of that member the search can see. Rename needs this. A find-references feature does not, and Roslyn's own features already avoid it:

- #25628 asked for a way to find references without cascading, and #42212 added the internal `Cascade` option.
- #40723 reported that Find All References on an override is too broad, and #51637 added the internal `UnidirectionalHierarchyCascade` option, which only finds references that could call into the member at runtime. Find All References, document highlighting, CodeLens, the inheritance margin and the stack trace explorer use it today.

#51637 kept existing clients, "like rename, or 3rd parties", on the old behavior, which is the right default. But `FindReferencesSearchOptions` and every overload that accepts it are internal, so a third party cannot opt in. I maintain the workspace side of an LSP server (csharp-ls), and the same applies to other language servers and code tools built on `MSBuildWorkspace`: they cannot return the results Visual Studio returns, and they pay for the full cascade on every request.

The cost grows with the solution. Find references on an override of a `System.Object` member, in three public solutions:

| Solution | Projects | Member | Unidirectional (internal) | Public API | Definitions (unidirectional / public) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| AvaloniaEdit (`AvaloniaEdit.slnx`) | 8 | `DocumentLine.ToString` | 0.16 s | 1.57 s | 3 / 556 |
| Polly (`Polly.slnx`) | 53 | `ResilienceEvent.ToString` | 0.76 s | 13.99 s | 18 / 1743 |
| Roslyn (`Compilers.slnf`) | 124 | `LineMapping.GetHashCode` | 1.27 s | 57.06 s | 7 / 2756 |

Measured with a small probe that calls the internal overload through reflection: `MSBuildWorkspace` (one project per target framework), Microsoft.CodeAnalysis 5.9.0, compilations built before timing, the order of the modes rotated over 3 runs, medians shown. The public API time stays the same on warm runs, so it is the cascade itself, not cold caches. On a mid-sized library like Polly that is 14 seconds per find-references request.

## Proposed API

```diff
 namespace Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.FindSymbols
 {
+    public enum FindReferencesCascadeMode
+    {
+        /// <summary>Current behavior of every existing overload: cascade up and down the
+        /// inheritance hierarchy from every symbol found, as rename needs.</summary>
+        Bidirectional = 0,
+        /// <summary>Cascade only to symbols whose references could call into the starting
+        /// symbol at runtime, as Find All References does.</summary>
+        Unidirectional = 1,
+        /// <summary>Do not cascade to related symbols.</summary>
+        None = 2,
+    }
+
-    internal readonly record struct FindReferencesSearchOptions
+    public readonly record struct FindReferencesSearchOptions
     {
+        public FindReferencesCascadeMode CascadeMode { get; init; }
     }
 
     public static partial class SymbolFinder
     {
+        public static Task<IEnumerable<ReferencedSymbol>> FindReferencesAsync(
+            ISymbol symbol,
+            Solution solution,
+            FindReferencesSearchOptions options,
+            IFindReferencesProgress? progress,
+            IImmutableSet<Document>? documents,
+            CancellationToken cancellationToken = default);
     }
 }
```

The type's existing members (`Cascade`, `UnidirectionalHierarchyCascade`, `Explicit`, `DisplayAllDefinitions`, `AssociatePropertyReferencesWithSpecificAccessor`) stay internal. `CascadeMode` maps onto the two cascade booleans: `Bidirectional` is today's `Default`, `Unidirectional` sets `UnidirectionalHierarchyCascade = true`, and `None` sets `Cascade = false`. Later public options become more members on the same type, without new overloads. Only the cancellation token is optional, to stay clear of RS0026 and RS0027.

## Usage Examples

```csharp
// textDocument/references in a language server: the same results Visual Studio's Find All References gives.
var options = new FindReferencesSearchOptions { CascadeMode = FindReferencesCascadeMode.Unidirectional };
var referencedSymbols = await SymbolFinder.FindReferencesAsync(
    symbol, solution, options, progress: null, documents: null, cancellationToken);
```

## Alternative Designs

- An enum parameter on the overload, without an options type. Every later option would need another overload.
- A separate public options type next to the internal one (the first version of this proposal, `FindReferencesOptions`). Two types for one concept.
- Making the two cascade booleans public instead of an enum. They allow a combination that means nothing (`Cascade = false` with `UnidirectionalHierarchyCascade = true`).
- No API: callers reach the internal overload through reflection, which breaks whenever its shape changes.

## Risks

- None for existing callers: it adds an overload and the existing ones keep their behavior.
- `default(FindReferencesSearchOptions)` has to behave like today's `Default`. That is why `Bidirectional` is the zero value of `FindReferencesCascadeMode`; the internal flags that default to `true` today (`Cascade`, `Explicit`) need the same care once the type is public.
- The unidirectional semantics become a public contract. The doc comment describes intent ("could call into the starting symbol at runtime") rather than the algorithm, to leave room to refine it.
- No change to the out-of-process path: the options are already sent to the remote host.

I can send the PR once the API is approved.

Issues.Title: SymbolFinder.FindReferencesAsync should not throw when a project has an UnresolvedAnalyzerReference
Issues.Body:
**Version Used**: Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp.Workspaces and Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Workspaces.MSBuild 5.12.0 (also 5.9.0). The code involved is unchanged on `main`. **Steps to Reproduce**: 1. Give a project an `UnresolvedAnalyzerReference`. `MSBuildWorkspace` creates one for every analyzer path that does not exist on disk, for example a generator referenced from a project that has not been built yet. 2. Call `SymbolFinder.FindReferencesAsync` on a member that overrides another one. No MSBuild needed: ```csharp var workspace = new AdhocWorkspace(); var project = workspace.AddProject("Lib", LanguageNames.CSharp) .AddMetadataReference(MetadataReference.CreateFromFile(typeof(object).Assembly.Location)) .AddAnalyzerReference(new UnresolvedAnalyzerReference("does-not-exist.dll")); project = project.AddDocument("Widget.cs", "public class Widget { public override string ToString() => \"widget\"; }").Project; var compilation = await project.GetCompilationAsync(); // works var toString = compilation!.GetTypeByMetadataName("Widget")!.GetMembers("ToString").Single(); await SymbolFinder.FindReferencesAsync(toString, project.Solution); // throws ``` The same happens with `MSBuildWorkspace`: a class library with `` and an override of `ToString`, a console project that references it, `OpenProjectAsync` on the console project, then `FindReferencesAsync` on the override. **Expected Behavior**: The search completes. An unresolved analyzer reference contributes no analyzers, so it should not affect find-references. `GetCompilationAsync`, hover and go-to-definition already work on the same project. **Actual Behavior**: `InvalidOperationException: Unexpected value 'Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Diagnostics.UnresolvedAnalyzerReference'`. Stack from 5.12.0, with the frames inside `ChecksumCache` and `ProducerConsumer` trimmed:
Stack trace ``` System.InvalidOperationException: Unexpected value 'Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Diagnostics.UnresolvedAnalyzerReference' of type 'Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Diagnostics.UnresolvedAnalyzerReference' at Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Serialization.SerializerService.CreateChecksum(AnalyzerReference reference) at Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Serialization.SerializerService.CreateChecksum(Object value, CancellationToken cancellationToken) ... at Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Serialization.ChecksumCache.GetOrCreateChecksumCollection[TReference](IReadOnlyList`1 references, ISerializerService serializer, CancellationToken cancellationToken) at Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.ProjectState.ComputeChecksumsAsync(CancellationToken cancellationToken) at Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.ProjectState.GetChecksumAsync(CancellationToken cancellationToken) at Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Diagnostics.Extensions.g__ComputeDiagnosticChecksumAsync|10_1(Project project, CancellationToken cancellationToken) at Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Diagnostics.Extensions.GetDiagnosticChecksumAsync(Project project, CancellationToken cancellationToken) at Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.FindSymbols.DependentTypeFinder.ProjectIndex.GetIndexAsync(Project project, CancellationToken cancellationToken) ... at Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.FindSymbols.DependentTypeFinder.DescendInheritanceTreeAsync(INamedTypeSymbol type, Solution solution, IImmutableSet`1 projects, Func`3 typeMatches, Func`2 shouldContinueSearching, Boolean transitive, CancellationToken cancellationToken) at Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.FindSymbols.DependentTypeFinder.FindDerivedClassesInCurrentProcessAsync(INamedTypeSymbol type, Solution solution, IImmutableSet`1 projects, Boolean transitive, CancellationToken cancellationToken) at Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.FindSymbols.DependentTypeFinder.FindTypesInCurrentProcessAsync(INamedTypeSymbol type, Solution solution, IImmutableSet`1 projects, Boolean transitive, DependentTypesKind kind, CancellationToken cancellationToken) at Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.FindSymbols.DependentTypeFinder.FindTypesAsync(INamedTypeSymbol type, Solution solution, IImmutableSet`1 projects, Boolean transitive, DependentTypesKind kind, CancellationToken cancellationToken) at Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.FindSymbols.SymbolFinder.FindDerivedClassesArrayAsync(INamedTypeSymbol type, Solution solution, Boolean transitive, IImmutableSet`1 projects, CancellationToken cancellationToken) at Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.FindSymbols.SymbolFinder.FindDerivedClassesAsync(INamedTypeSymbol type, Solution solution, Boolean transitive, IImmutableSet`1 projects, CancellationToken cancellationToken) at Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.FindSymbols.SymbolFinder.FindImplementedInterfaceMembersArrayAsync(ISymbol symbol, Solution solution, IImmutableSet`1 projects, Boolean includeImplementationsThroughDerivedTypes, CancellationToken cancellationToken) at Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.FindSymbols.FindReferencesSearchEngine.SymbolSet.AddUpSymbolsAsync(FindReferencesSearchEngine engine, ISymbol symbol, MetadataUnifyingSymbolHashSet seenSymbols, ArrayBuilder`1 workQueue, ImmutableHashSet`1 projects, Boolean includeImplementationsThroughDerivedTypes, CancellationToken cancellationToken) at Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.FindSymbols.FindReferencesSearchEngine.SymbolSet.DetermineInitialUpSymbolsAsync(FindReferencesSearchEngine engine, MetadataUnifyingSymbolHashSet initialSymbols, Boolean includeImplementationsThroughDerivedTypes, CancellationToken cancellationToken) at Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.FindSymbols.FindReferencesSearchEngine.SymbolSet.CreateAsync(FindReferencesSearchEngine engine, MetadataUnifyingSymbolHashSet symbols, Boolean includeImplementationsThroughDerivedTypes, CancellationToken cancellationToken) at Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.FindSymbols.FindReferencesSearchEngine.PerformSearchAsync(ImmutableArray`1 symbols, Action`1 onReferenceFound, CancellationToken cancellationToken) ... at Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.FindSymbols.FindReferencesSearchEngine.FindReferencesAsync(ImmutableArray`1 symbols, CancellationToken cancellationToken) at Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.FindSymbols.SymbolFinder.FindReferencesAsync(ISymbol symbol, Solution solution, IStreamingFindReferencesProgress progress, IImmutableSet`1 documents, FindReferencesSearchOptions options, CancellationToken cancellationToken) at Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.FindSymbols.SymbolFinder.FindReferencesAsync(ISymbol symbol, Solution solution, FindReferencesSearchOptions options, CancellationToken cancellationToken) at Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.FindSymbols.SymbolFinder.FindReferencesAsync(ISymbol symbol, Solution solution, CancellationToken cancellationToken) ```
I ran into this in an LSP server (csharp-ls), and again when loading `Compilers.slnf` from a restored but unbuilt clone of this repository: the projects that reference generators as project references carry unresolved analyzer references until the generators are built. **Impact**: other tools built on `MSBuildWorkspace` have hit the same crash and patched around it on their side: mrpmorris/Roslynk#66, Atypical-Consulting/RoselineMCP#242 (151 of 951 tool calls failing), CodeBoarding/CodeBoarding#603, glidermcp/glidermcp#61, JaneySprings/DotRush#140.
Cause: how find-references reaches the throw - `MSBuildProjectLoader.Worker.ResolveAnalyzerReferences` turns an analyzer path that does not exist into an `UnresolvedAnalyzerReference`. - For an override, find-references cascades up the hierarchy and calls `FindDerivedClassesAsync`. `DependentTypeFinder.ProjectIndex.GetIndexAsync` caches its per-project index under `GetDiagnosticChecksumAsync`, which includes `ProjectState.GetChecksumAsync`, which checksums every analyzer reference of the project. - `SerializerService.CreateChecksum(AnalyzerReference)` in `src/Workspaces/Core/Portable/Serialization/SerializerService_Reference.cs` handles `AnalyzerFileReference`, `AnalyzerImageReference` and `IAnalyzerReferenceWithGuid`. Anything else reaches `throw ExceptionUtilities.UnexpectedValue(reference)`.
**Workaround**: Strip the unresolved references before searching. They contribute no analyzers, so the results are unchanged: ```csharp foreach (var project in solution.Projects) solution = solution.WithProjectAnalyzerReferences( project.Id, project.AnalyzerReferences.Where(r => r is not UnresolvedAnalyzerReference)); ``` **Proposed fix**: I have a change with tests ready and would like your preference on the direction before opening a PR: 1. Add an `UnresolvedAnalyzerReference` case to `CreateChecksum` that writes a type marker and the unresolved path. The checksum stays stable while the reference is unresolved and differs from an `AnalyzerFileReference` to the same path. This matches how a missing file behind an `AnalyzerFileReference` is already handled: `TryGetFileReferenceMvid` returns `Guid.Empty` instead of throwing. The out-of-process serialization (`WriteAnalyzerReferenceTo` / `ReadAnalyzerReferenceFrom`) stays as it is. As far as I can tell, the hosts that sync to the out-of-process service create `AnalyzerFileReference` even for missing files, so they never send it an unresolved reference. 2. The same, plus `UnresolvedAnalyzerReference` support in that serialization, so a project holding one could also be synced out of process. The first is the change I have: a few lines in `SerializerService_Reference.cs` plus tests in `Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Workspaces.UnitTests`.

Issues.Title: Prevent PublishContainer telemetry failures for four-part framework versions
Issues.Body:
`PublishContainer` failed for `net481` projects because telemetry attempted to parse the generated `4.8.1.0` framework version as strict SemVer. This occurred even when `ContainerBaseImage` was explicitly provided.

- **Telemetry parsing**
  - Use non-throwing `NuGetVersion.TryParse`, which accepts four-part versions.
  - Omit the telemetry framework value when parsing fails rather than failing the build.

```csharp
NuGetVersion.TryParse(semver, out var version)
    ? $"{version.Major}.{version.Minor}"
    : null;
```

- **Regression coverage**
  - Exercise `ComputeContainerBaseImage` for `net481`.
  - Verify the user-provided .NET Framework base image passes through unchanged.

<!-- START COPILOT CODING AGENT SUFFIX -->

- Fixes #57367

Issues.Title: extend CA2249 to span IndexOf, IndexOfAny and IndexOfAnyExcept
Issues.Body:
fixes dotnet/runtime#87691

as approved in API review, CA2249 now also flags span searches only compared with 0 or -1, and the fixer swaps in the matching Contains:
- `span.IndexOf(x) >= 0` → `span.Contains(x)`
- `span.IndexOfAny(x, y) < 0` → `!span.ContainsAny(x, y)`
- `span.IndexOfAnyExcept(x, y) != -1` → `span.ContainsAnyExcept(x, y)`

tested: 31 new C# and VB tests (24 fail without this change), and a run over runtime's CoreLib and libraries: 8 hits, all correct.

Issues.Title: [release/11.0.2xx] Mark NETSdkError, NETSdkWarning, and NETSdkInformation as multithreadable
Issues.Body:
Marks the three shared `MessageBase` tasks in `src/Tasks/Common/` with `[MSBuildMultiThreadableTask]`:

- `NETSdkError` / `NETBuildExtensionsError` (`src/Tasks/Common/NETSdkError.cs`)
- `NETSdkWarning` / `NETBuildExtensionsWarning` (`src/Tasks/Common/NETSdkWarning.cs`)
- `NETSdkInformation` / `NETBuildExtensionsInformation` (`src/Tasks/Common/NETSdkInformation.cs`)

These tasks only format resource strings and log messages via `MessageBase` without accessing paths or environment variables, so `IMultiThreadableTask` is not needed.

Verified by building both `Microsoft.NET.Build.Tasks` and `Microsoft.NET.Build.Extensions.Tasks` across all TFMs (`net11.0` and `net472`).

Issues.Title: Mark remaining pure in-memory tasks as multithreadable
Issues.Body:
Marks 7 pure in-memory shipping MSBuild tasks (SetGeneratedAppConfigMetadata, ResolveStaticWebAssetsEffectiveTargetFramework, ComputeDotnetBaseImageAndTag, ParseContainerProperties, ValidateParameter, GetPassword, NormalizeServiceUrl) with [MSBuildMultiThreadableTask] so they run in-process under MSBuild -mt instead of routing to an out-of-proc TaskHost.

None of these tasks access files, process CWD, environment variables, or mutable static state. See [Update a task for multithreaded mode](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/visualstudio/msbuild/update-task-multithreaded).

Companion PR for elease/11.0.2xx: #57373. Relates to dotnet/msbuild#11835.

Issues.Body:
### Describe the bug

#### Failure

The Helix work item containing `DotnetNewInstantiateTests.CanInstantiateTemplate_WithConditionallyEnabledParams` crashed with status `BadExit` on Azure Linux 4 x64, interrupting PR validation. The available report does not include an exit code, assertion failure, or crash stack.

### Steps to reproduce

No local reproduction is established. See [build 1697426, run 47395878, result 105035](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1697426&view=ms.vss-test-web.build-test-results-tab&runId=47395878&resultId=105035&paneView=debug) and the [linked work-item console](https://helixr1107v0xdeko0k025g8.blob.core.windows.net/dotnet-sdk-refs-pull-57196-merge-972ea1b1a1214fd0a6/dotnet-new.IntegrationTests.dll.3/1/console.1cb0b881.log?helixlogtype=result). Both Azure DevOps and the console host failed DNS on two retrieval attempts from the automated investigation host.

### Expected behavior

The work item runs the conditional-parameter template test and reports its result without a process-level crash.

### Actual behavior

Build Analysis reports: `This is a helix work item crash with status: BadExit.` The failing configuration is `Linux x64 run on azurelinux.4.amd64.open (attempt 1)`. The latest Build Insights snapshot reports a 0.067% failure rate; its denominator and time range are not available here.

### Is this a regression?

Unknown. A later green pipeline check and green Build Analysis still retain the same failed result, so successful test recovery and nondeterminism are not established. This is an unresolved CI failure, not a confirmed root cause or confirmed flake.

### Are there any workarounds?

None verified. No CI retry was triggered by this investigation.

### dotnet --info output

Unavailable from retained evidence.

### IDE version

N/A (CI).

### Other details

#### Possible cause

Unknown. `BadExit` is a work-item status, not enough to distinguish a test-host crash, a failing child command, or another work-item problem. The [test at the PR's final head](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/blob/30520dc2625b039559cb9856f807e18ae38aca8e/test/dotnet-new.IntegrationTests/DotnetNewInstantiateTests.Approval.cs#L702-L726) installs a test template into isolated directories, invokes `dotnet new`, checks exit code zero and empty stderr, and verifies generated content. No retained evidence identifies which operation failed or which data row was running; associating this work-item crash with a specific assertion would be speculative.

#### Affected builds and PRs

| PR | PR target branch | Build(s) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| [dotnet/sdk#57196](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/pull/57196) | `main` | [1697426 failed result](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1697426&view=ms.vss-test-web.build-test-results-tab&runId=47395878&resultId=105035), first reported 2026-11-24T17:30Z; later green checks still contain this failure | `dotnet-new.IntegrationTests.dll.3`, `CanInstantiateTemplate_WithConditionallyEnabledParams`; Linux x64 `azurelinux.4.amd64.open`, reported attempt 1. Final PR head `30520dc2625b039559cb9856f807e18ae38aca8e`. Per-attempt timeline and compiled merge inputs remain unverified. |

Decision: unresolved, no prototype. One observed work-item crash and an unavailable console do not identify a safe causal correction. Retrying blindly, extending deadlines, or relaxing assertions would not explain this failure. The next useful evidence is the original console, test-host exit/crash details, and attempt timeline; current recurrence and retry cost beyond the report are unknown. No behavior-matching issue or PR was found in all-state dotnet/sdk searches or existing fork tracking issues.

Issues.Title: dotnetup default macOS install path (`~/Library/Application Support/dotnetup/dotnet`) contains a space and breaks Android AOT, WASM AOT, and iOS Run targets
Issues.Body:
## Summary

On macOS, `dotnetup` installs the .NET SDK and workload packs under `~/Library/Application Support/dotnetup/dotnet` by default. Because `Application Support` contains a space, any SDK target, workload wrapper script, or native AOT tool that invokes a path via `sh` without quoting fails with `No such file or directory` (`/Users/<user>/Library/Application: No such file or directory` or `/Users/<user>/Library/as: No such file or directory`).

While individual workload scripts/tools should quote paths properly, having a space in the default `DOTNET_ROOT` on macOS breaks standard out-of-the-box .NET workflows across Android, MAUI, WebAssembly, and iOS. Using a space-free default path on macOS (for example `~/.dotnetup/dotnet` next to the `dotnetup` binary at `~/.dotnetup/dotnetup`, or `~/.local/share/dotnetup/dotnet`) would avoid this entire class of failures, while the underlying workload tools are also fixed to quote paths with spaces.

---

## Concrete Failures Triggered by `~/Library/Application Support/dotnetup/dotnet`

### 1. Android Release / AOT builds fail in `Microsoft.Android.Sdk.Darwin` binutils wrapper scripts

Building any Android or .NET MAUI Android project in `Release` configuration (where Mono AOT is enabled by default) fails when running the binutils wrapper scripts under `packs/Microsoft.Android.Sdk.Darwin/<version>/tools/Darwin/binutils/bin/`:

- `aarch64-linux-android-as`
- `aarch64-linux-android-ld`
- `aarch64-linux-android-strip`
- `arm-linux-androideabi-as` / `ld` / `strip`
- `i686-linux-android-as` / `ld` / `strip`
- `x86_64-linux-android-as` / `ld` / `strip`

Each wrapper script contains an unquoted `$(dirname $0)`:

```sh
#!/bin/bash -e
MY_NAME="$(basename $0)"
MY_DIR="$(cd $(dirname $0);pwd)"

exec "${MY_DIR}"/as @gas-arch=${MY_NAME} "$@"
```

Because `$(dirname $0)` is unquoted, bash word-splits `/Users/<user>/Library/Application Support/dotnetup/...` into `/Users/<user>/Library/Application` and `Support/...`, causing `cd` to land in `/Users/<user>/Library` (or fail) and producing:

```text
Microsoft.Android.Sdk.Aot.targets(123,5): error : /Users/<user>/Library/Application Support/dotnetup/dotnet/packs/Microsoft.Android.Sdk.Darwin/36.1.118/tools/Darwin/binutils/bin/aarch64-linux-android-as: line 5: /Users/<user>/Library/as: No such file or directory
Microsoft.Android.Sdk.Aot.targets(123,5): error : AOT of image obj/Release/net10.0-android/android-arm64/linked/SkiaSharp.dll failed.
```

### 2. WebAssembly AOT (`RunAOTCompilation=true`) fails in `mono-aot-cross` (`compile-in-child` and `llvm-path`)

Publishing any `Microsoft.NET.Sdk.WebAssembly` or `Microsoft.NET.Sdk.BlazorWebAssembly` project with `<RunAOTCompilation>true</RunAOTCompilation>` fails in `_WasmAotCompileApp` (`WasmApp.Common.targets`):

1. `WasmApp.Common.targets` passes `compile-in-child` (on non-Windows) and `LLVMPath="$(_WasmLLVMPathForAOT)"` to `MonoAOTCompiler`.
2. When `compile-in-child` is enabled, `mono-aot-cross` spawns child processes via `sh -c` without quoting its own executable path (`~/Library/Application Support/dotnetup/dotnet/packs/Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.AOT.osx-arm64.Cross.browser-wasm/<version>/tools/mono-aot-cross`).
3. `mono-aot-cross` also invokes LLVM tools (`opt` / `llc`) under `llvm-path=/Users/<user>/Library/Application Support/dotnetup/dotnet/packs/Microsoft.NET.Runtime.Emscripten.<version>.Sdk.osx-arm64/<version>/tools/bin/` via `sh -c` without quoting the path.

Both fail with:

```text
WasmApp.Common.targets(672,5): error : Precompiling failed for obj/Release/net10.0/wasm/for-publish/aot-in/System.Private.CoreLib.dll with exit code 1.
WasmApp.Common.targets(672,5): error : Executing: /Users/<user>/Library/Application Support/dotnetup/dotnet/packs/Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.AOT.osx-arm64.Cross.browser-wasm/10.0.15/Sdk/../tools/mono-aot-cross "--wasm-exceptions" "--debug" "--llvm" "--aot=no-opt,static,direct-icalls,deterministic,_child,mattr=simd,nodebug,llvm-path=/Users/<user>/Library/Application Support/dotnetup/dotnet/packs/Microsoft.NET.Runtime.Emscripten.3.1.56.Sdk.osx-arm64/10.0.15/tools/bin/,..."
WasmApp.Common.targets(672,5): error : sh: /Users/<user>/Library/Application: No such file or directory
```

### 3. Emscripten native relinking (`WasmBuildNative=true`) wrapper scripts

In `Microsoft.NET.Runtime.Emscripten.*.Sdk.osx-arm64` (e.g., 10.0.14), wrapper scripts in `tools/bin/clang` used unquoted `CLANG_CC=$(dirname $0)/clang-19`, failing when `WasmBuildNative=true`:

```text
.../tools/bin/clang: line 25: /Users/<user>/Library: No such file or directory
```

### 4. Apple `dotnet build -t:Run` (`RunCommand` unquoted in `<Exec>`)

Tracked in #57310 / #54917: `Microsoft.Sdk.Mobile.targets` sets `<RunCommand>$(MlaunchPath)</RunCommand>` (pointing into `~/Library/Application Support/dotnetup/dotnet/packs/Microsoft.iOS.Sdk.../tools/bin/mlaunch`) and `Microsoft.NET.Sdk.targets` runs `<Exec Command="$(RunCommand) $(RunArguments)" />` without quotes, failing with:

```text
/Users/<user>/Library/Application: No such file or directory
```

---

## Recommendations

1. **Change `dotnetup`'s default macOS install root to a path without spaces** (for example `~/.dotnetup/dotnet`, alongside `~/.dotnetup/dotnetup`, or `~/.dotnet/dotnetup`), and support persisting custom install paths in `dotnetup` config (#55346).
2. **Fix the unquoted paths in the workload packs/tools** so SDK paths with spaces also work:
   - Quote `"$(dirname "$0")"` in `Microsoft.Android.Sdk.Darwin`'s `tools/Darwin/binutils/bin/*` wrapper scripts (`dotnet/android`).
   - Quote the child compiler and `llvm-path` command invocations in `mono-aot-cross` (`dotnet/runtime`).

Issues.Title: dotnet test cannot launch test executables from long paths on Windows
Issues.Body:
`dotnet build` succeeds, but `dotnet test` fails before running tests when the executable path exceeds 260 characters. Reproduced with both **xUnit and MSTest**, using Microsoft.Testing.Platform **2.5.3**.

**Reproduction:** Run from a short directory on Windows with .NET SDK 11.0.100 and long paths enabled.

```powershell
$root = Join-Path (Get-Location) 'PathLaunchRepro'
$name = 'LongName' * 15
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path "$root\$name" | Out-Null
Set-Location $root

'{"sdk":{"version":"11.0.100"},"test":{"runner":"Microsoft.Testing.Platform"}}' |
    Set-Content global.json
'<Project />' | Set-Content Directory.Build.props
'<Project />' | Set-Content Directory.Packages.props
@'
<Project Sdk="MSTest.Sdk/4.2.3">
  <PropertyGroup>
    <TargetFramework>net11.0</TargetFramework>
  </PropertyGroup>
  <ItemGroup>
    <PackageReference Include="Microsoft.Testing.Platform" Version="2.5.3" />
    <PackageReference Include="Microsoft.Testing.Platform.MSBuild" Version="2.5.3" />
  </ItemGroup>
</Project>
'@ | Set-Content "$name\$name.csproj"
@'
using Microsoft.VisualStudio.TestTools.UnitTesting;

[TestClass]
public class ExampleTests
{
    [TestMethod]
    public void Example() => Assert.IsTrue(true);
}
'@ | Set-Content "$name\ExampleTests.cs"

dotnet build "$name\$name.csproj"
dotnet test --project "$name\$name.csproj"
```

**Expected:** The test runs.

**Actual:** `Win32Exception (206): The filename or extension is too long`. Running the built DLL directly with `dotnet` succeeds.

Possibly related to https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/58492.

Issues.Title: `PublishContainer` fails for `net481`: `'4.8.1.0' is not a valid version string` in `ComputeDotnetBaseImageAndTag`
Issues.Body:
### Describe the bug

Running `dotnet publish /t:PublishContainer` on a project that targets `net481` fails, even when `ContainerBaseImage` is set explicitly. The `ComputeDotnetBaseImageAndTag` task throws because it gets a four-part version (`4.8.1.0`) that `NuGet.Versioning.SemanticVersion.Parse` can't read.

The failure happens while the task logs telemetry. Base-image inference isn't involved, since the user already supplied the image.

### To Reproduce

1. A project with `<TargetFramework>net481</TargetFramework>` and `<OutputType>Exe</OutputType>`.
2. Run:
   ```
   dotnet publish -c Release -r win-x64 --self-contained /t:PublishContainer ^
     -p:ContainerBaseImage=mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/framework/runtime:4.8.1-windowsservercore-ltsc2022 ^
     -p:ContainerRepository=myapp ^
     -p:ContainerArchiveOutputPath=out/image.tar.gz
   ```

### Expected behavior

Since `ContainerBaseImage` is set, the task should return it unchanged and the container should be built.

### Actual behavior

```
Microsoft.NET.Build.Containers.targets(53,5): error MSB4018: The "ComputeDotnetBaseImageAndTag" task failed unexpectedly.
System.ArgumentException: '4.8.1.0' is not a valid version string. (Parameter 'value')
   at NuGet.Versioning.SemanticVersion.Parse(String value)
   at Microsoft.NET.Build.Containers.Tasks.ComputeDotnetBaseImageAndTag.ParseSemVerToMajorMinor(String semver) in ComputeDotnetBaseImageAndTag.cs:line 345
   at Microsoft.NET.Build.Containers.Tasks.ComputeDotnetBaseImageAndTag.LogNoInferencePerformedTelemetry() in ComputeDotnetBaseImageAndTag.cs:line 331
   at Microsoft.NET.Build.Containers.Tasks.ComputeDotnetBaseImageAndTag.Execute() in ComputeDotnetBaseImageAndTag.cs:line 103
```

### Root cause

In `Microsoft.NET.Build.Containers.targets`, the `ComputeContainerBaseImage` target passes:

```xml
<ComputeDotnetBaseImageAndTag
    UserBaseImage="$(ContainerBaseImage)"
    TargetFrameworkVersion="$(_TargetFrameworkVersionWithoutV).0"
    ... />
```

Appending `.0` assumes `_TargetFrameworkVersionWithoutV` always has two parts:

| TFM | `_TargetFrameworkVersionWithoutV` | Passed value | `SemanticVersion.Parse` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `net8.0` | `8.0` | `8.0.0` | OK |
| `net48` | `4.8` | `4.8.0` | OK |
| `net481` | `4.8.1` | `4.8.1.0` | **throws** |
| `net462` / `net472` | `4.6.2` / `4.7.2` | `4.6.2.0` / `4.7.2.0` | **throws** |

In `ComputeDotnetBaseImageAndTag.cs`:

- `Execute()` calls `LogNoInferencePerformedTelemetry()` when `UserBaseImage` is set.
- That method calls `ParseSemVerToMajorMinor(TargetFrameworkVersion)`, which uses the strict `SemanticVersion.Parse(semver)`.
- The exception escapes `Execute()`, so publishing fails with MSB4018. Collecting telemetry shouldn't be able to fail a build.

`ComputeVersionPart()` uses `SemanticVersion.TryParse` instead, so the inference path handles this case. Only the telemetry paths (`LogNoInferencePerformedTelemetry` and `LogInferencePerformedTelemetry`) use the throwing `Parse`.

### Suggested fix (any of these)

1. In the targets, pass the version without blindly adding `.0`. For example, normalize it with `$([System.Version]::Parse(...))`, or only append `.0` when the value has two parts.
2. In `ParseSemVerToMajorMinor`, use `NuGet.Versioning.NuGetVersion.TryParse`, which accepts four-part versions, or `System.Version.TryParse`. Fall back to the raw string or `null` when parsing fails.
3. Wrap telemetry collection in a try/catch so it can never fail the build.

### Workaround

Add these targets to the project (or `Directory.Build.targets`). They temporarily shorten `_TargetFrameworkVersionWithoutV` to `major.minor` for the container base-image computation, then restore it:

```xml
<!-- SDK container targets pass "$(_TargetFrameworkVersionWithoutV).0" to a strict SemVer parser;
     "4.8.1.0" (net481) fails, so expose a 2-part version only for that task. -->
<Target Name="_FixNetFxVersionForContainerBaseImage"
        BeforeTargets="ComputeContainerBaseImage"
        Condition="'$(TargetFrameworkIdentifier)' == '.NETFramework'">
  <PropertyGroup>
    <_OriginalTargetFrameworkVersionWithoutV>$(_TargetFrameworkVersionWithoutV)</_OriginalTargetFrameworkVersionWithoutV>
    <_TargetFrameworkVersionWithoutV>$([System.Version]::Parse('$(_TargetFrameworkVersionWithoutV)').ToString(2))</_TargetFrameworkVersionWithoutV>
  </PropertyGroup>
</Target>

<Target Name="_RestoreNetFxVersionAfterContainerBaseImage"
        AfterTargets="ComputeContainerBaseImage"
        Condition="'$(_OriginalTargetFrameworkVersionWithoutV)' != ''">
  <PropertyGroup>
    <_TargetFrameworkVersionWithoutV>$(_OriginalTargetFrameworkVersionWithoutV)</_TargetFrameworkVersionWithoutV>
  </PropertyGroup>
</Target>
```

With this, the task receives `4.8.0`, which parses, and the user-supplied `ContainerBaseImage` is passed through unchanged.

### Environment

- .NET SDK: 11.0.100
- Target framework: `net481`, RID `win-x64`, self-contained
- Base image: `mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/framework/runtime:4.8.1-windowsservercore-ltsc2022`
- CI: Azure Pipelines, `DotNetCoreCLI@2` task (2.281.1), Windows agent

Issues.Title: Bump the github-actions group with 3 updates

Changelog

[Unreleased] - ReleaseDate

[2.0.0] - 2026-11-16

Added

  • Release binary for macOS on Intel (mlc-x86_64-apple-darwin)

Changed

  • The GitHub Action is a composite action which downloads the release binary instead of a Docker container action. It runs on Linux, Windows and macOS runners, including ubuntu-slim which is recommended to save runner costs. The Docker image on Docker Hub is still published

[1.3.0] - 2026-10-20

Added

  • --quiet / -q option (and quiet in .mlc.toml) which only prints warnings, errors and the summary. The banner and all links which are ok or skipped are left out
  • --format json option (and format = "json" in .mlc.toml) which prints a single JSON document with the summary and all issues to stdout. Debug output goes to stderr in this mode
  • Documentation for AI agents and automation: README section, AGENTS.md, llms.txt and ready to copy examples for AGENTS.md, Claude Code hooks and skills, and pre-commit

Changed

  • Rust edition 2024. Building from source needs Rust 1.88 or newer, which is checked in CI
  • Invalid arguments (for example --throttle abc or an unknown markup type) and an invalid .mlc.toml print an error and exit with code 2 instead of panicking. The same exit code is used for an invalid --root-dir, which used to be 1
  • Failing to write the --csv file prints an error instead of panicking. A web link which is not a valid URL is reported as broken link instead of panicking
  • The banner is not printed anymore when --help or an invalid argument is passed
  • Warnings about not existing paths passed via --files or --ignore-path are printed to stderr instead of stdout
  • The CSV report and the list of broken links are sorted (errors first, then by file, line and column) instead of depending on which web request finished first
  • Library: mlc::run returns Result<(), mlc::Error>, the Display implementation of Config, the glob re-export of colored and the async-ness of link_validator::resolve_target_link are gone, logger::init takes a second use_stderr argument and MarkupType::file_extensions returns a slice
  • The release binary is much smaller (release profile with LTO, opt-level = "s", panic = "abort" and stripped symbols, and the unused code above). This means faster downloads in CI and a faster start
  • The docker image is based on Alpine Linux instead of Ubuntu and is about 10 times smaller. The entrypoint.sh of the GitHub Action uses sh instead of bash

Fixed

  • gitignore = false and gituntracked = false in .mlc.toml enabled the options. Now they are only enabled with true
  • --gitignore and --gituntracked now also recognize the markup files with extensions like .markdown or .htm and upper case extensions
