Issues.Title: Prevent Aspire log notification test hangs
Issues.Body:
`SendLogMessageAsync_Test` could send before Kestrel registered the client WebSocket, dropping the notification and waiting until Helix’s 48-minute timeout.

- **Synchronize connection readiness**
  - Wait for server-side socket registration after the client handshake.
  - Surface connection failures through the awaited readiness task.

- **Bound notification delivery**
  - Fail after five seconds if the expected log notification is not received.

```csharp
await aspireServer.WaitForSocketConnectionAsync(DcpId, cancellationToken)
    .WaitAsync(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(5), cancellationToken);
```

- **Current build:** [dotnet-sdk-public-ci 20261125.12](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/cbb18261-c48f-4abb-8651-8cdcb5474649/_build/results?buildId=1699673)

- **Phase:** `test-execution`
- **Failure type:** `timeout`
- **Evidence sources:** `helix-console`, `process-exit-code`, `helix-trx`, `helix-dump`
- **Failure fingerprint:** `test-execution|timeout|microsoft.webtools.aspireservice.tests.dll|hang-dump-timeout-of-<n>-<n>-<n>-expired-the-following-tests-were-still-running-when-dump-was-taken-format-<time-elapsed-since-start>-<name>-test-host-crashed-recovered-<n>-test-re`

## Failure History

The same stable fingerprint is present in the current build and at least three earlier builds from different `main` commits: 1698714 (`6ca6788`), 1698909 (`a2dd4f5`), 1699437 (`082ed9a`), and 1699673 (`7a6b95d`). The surrounding pipeline sequence was: 1698060 pass, 1698714 fail, 1698909 fail, 1699437 fail, 1699673 fail, then 1700013 pass. This establishes recurrence, not the underlying cause.

## Error Details

Exact excerpt: `Hang dump timeout of '00:48:00' expired; Test host crashed; recovered 13 test result(s) from the TRX streaming sidecar; Test application process didn't exit gracefully, exit code is '137'; [00:48:01] SendLogMessageAsync_Test`. The work item monitor reported exit code `7`.

- [Console log](https://helix.dot.net/api/jobs/85289432-bfae-44cc-a005-c058b6eb6362/workitems/Microsoft.WebTools.AspireService.Tests.dll/files/console.9151a128.log?api-version=2019-06-17)
- [Hang dump](https://helix.dot.net/api/jobs/85289432-bfae-44cc-a005-c058b6eb6362/workitems/Microsoft.WebTools.AspireService.Tests.dll/files/dotnet_14219_hang.dmp?api-version=2019-06-17)
- [TRX result](https://helix.dot.net/api/jobs/85289432-bfae-44cc-a005-c058b6eb6362/workitems/Microsoft.WebTools.AspireService.Tests.dll/files/Microsoft.WebTools.AspireService.Tests_net12.0_x64.trx?api-version=2019-06-17)

The TRX summary reports 13 executed and 13 passed tests; no named assertion result establishes why `SendLogMessageAsync_Test` remained active.

## Root Cause Analysis

- **Observed:** The test host remained active at `SendLogMessageAsync_Test` until the 48-minute hang-dump timeout, then exited with host code 137 and the work item ended with exit code 7. A full dump was successfully captured.
- **Assessment:** The evidence establishes a recurring test-host hang or termination during that test, but does not establish whether the proximate cause is a deadlock, blocked I/O, resource pressure, or another process/runtime condition. The generic `Monitor Helix Jobs` failure and its artifact cascade are downstream effects, not causes.
- **Confidence:** **Medium** for the recurring hang pattern; **Low** for its underlying cause.
- **Alternatives / Unknowns:** Dump stacks, process/resource state, and the test's service/logging interactions have not been analyzed. The collector does not establish whether this is SDK code, an external service dependency, or Linux host/resource behavior.

## Suggested Investigation

1. Analyze the captured hang dump for blocked threads, locks, waits, and child processes around `SendLogMessageAsync_Test`; correlate with the console log and TRX.
2. Inspect the test implementation and logging/service shutdown path for an uncompleted async operation or missing cancellation.
3. Compare a failing build with the nearest passing build and target-branch behavior, then check whether the failure correlates with Linux host/resource conditions.

Historical context: closed issues [#56131](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/issues/56131) and [#55477](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/issues/55477) describe materially similar AspireService hangs, but no open issue covers the current fingerprint.

Issues.Body:
`dotnet watch` generated invalid temporary solutions when multiple root projects shared a filename, causing builds to fail before project evaluation.

  ```xml
    <Project Path="src/Orders/Api.csproj" />
  </Folder>
  <Folder Name="/2/">
    <Project Path="src/Billing/Api.csproj" />
  </Folder>
  ```

- **Regression coverage**
  - Verify same-named projects retain their paths and receive unique solution folders.

Issues.Title: dotnet watch: building several projects fails when two of them have the same file name (temporary solution rejects duplicate project names)
Issues.Body:
### Describe the bug

When the watcher builds more than one root project, it writes the roots into a temporary solution (the workaround for https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/issues/51311). A solution needs distinct project names within a solution folder, so two roots with the same file name in different directories, for example `src/Orders/Api.csproj` and `src/Billing/Api.csproj`, make every build fail before it starts:

```text
/tmp/dotnet-watch-giISy3/1.slnx(3,4): error MSB4025: The project file could not be loaded. Microsoft.VisualStudio.SolutionPersistence.Model.SolutionException: Project name 'Api' already exists in the 'Root' solution folder.
```

The watcher then waits for a file change ("Fix the error to continue"), but the error is in a file it generated, so no edit to the projects fixes it.

### Cause

[`HotReloadDotNetWatcher`](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/blob/7a6b95d17bde142343a81adcd7cc27bd5bbd3be0/src/Dotnet.Watch/Watch/HotReload/HotReloadDotNetWatcher.cs#L1199-L1209) adds each project path as a `<Project Path="..." />` directly under `<Solution>`. [`SolutionModel.ValidateProjectName`](https://github.com/microsoft/vs-solutionpersistence/blob/21e6c361ea088e94f4b97b8859625c62eb5bad36/src/Microsoft.VisualStudio.SolutionPersistence/Model/SolutionModel.cs#L583-L605) rejects a project whose display name (the file name without its extension, compared case-insensitively) already exists in the same solution folder.

This affects `Microsoft.DotNet.HotReload.Watch.Aspire` 10.0.403 and 11.0.100, and `main` as of 7a6b95d17bde142343a81adcd7cc27bd5bbd3be0.

### Repro

1. Create two console projects with the same file name in different directories: `a/Api.csproj` and `b/Api.csproj`.
2. Start the Aspire watch server for both projects. For example, run an Aspire AppHost with `aspire run --watch` that adds both projects as resources, with an Aspire build that doesn't exclude such groups.
3. The initial build fails with the error above.

### Suggested fix

Do either of the following:

- put each project in its own solution folder in the temporary solution (for example `<Folder Name="/1/"><Project Path="..." /></Folder>`), because names need to be unique only within a folder;
- build same-named projects individually, as the watcher already does when a global `RuntimeIdentifier` is set.

### Workaround

Rename one of the projects. Aspire detects such watch groups and runs their services without watching.

Issues.Title: dotnet watch (Aspire server): launching a web project fails with "The given key '1021' was not present in the dictionary" when browser tools are disabled
Issues.Body:
### Describe the bug

With `Microsoft.DotNet.HotReload.Watch.Aspire` 11.0.100 (dotnet/dotnet 297acf930fb0f5c07fd4e51d78e521b4ad2e5d1f), every launch of a web project whose Hot Reload browser tools are off fails:

```text
aspire watch server ❌ Failed to start '/src/Api/Api.csproj': The given key '1021' was not present in the dictionary.
```

Browser tools are off when `BrowserToolsBuildOutputs.FromProjectSettings` returns null, for example:

- a non-Debug configuration without `EnableHotReloadInRuntimeConfigDevFile=true`;
- `StaticWebAssetsEnabled` or `JSModulesEnabled` set to `false`.

### Cause

[`BrowserToolsBuildOutputsExtensions.FromProject`](https://github.com/dotnet/dotnet/blob/297acf930fb0f5c07fd4e51d78e521b4ad2e5d1f/src/sdk/src/Dotnet.Watch/Watch/Browser/BrowserToolsBuildOutputsExtensions.cs#L31-L33) logs `LogEvents.BrowserToolsNotSupportedByProjectSettings`. `HotReloadClient`'s `LogEvents` allocates IDs from 1000, so this warning is `EventId` 1021.

The watcher's `LoggerFactory.Logger.Log` ([IReporter.cs#L107](https://github.com/dotnet/dotnet/blob/297acf930fb0f5c07fd4e51d78e521b4ad2e5d1f/src/sdk/src/Dotnet.Watch/Watch/UI/IReporter.cs#L107)) calls `MessageDescriptor.GetDescriptor(eventId)` for every non-zero `EventId`. That method indexes `s_descriptors` directly. `BrowserToolsNotSupportedByProjectSettings` is not mirrored into a `MessageDescriptor`, so logging the warning throws `KeyNotFoundException`. `ProcessLauncherFactory.HandleRequestAsync` reports that exception as the launch failure.

The same code is on `release/11.0.1xx` and on `main`: as of 7a6b95d17bde142343a81adcd7cc27bd5bbd3be0, [SharedSecretBuildOutputsExtensions.cs#L31](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/blob/7a6b95d17bde142343a81adcd7cc27bd5bbd3be0/src/Dotnet.Watch/Watch/Browser/SharedSecretBuildOutputsExtensions.cs#L31) logs the event and [IReporter.cs#L170-L171](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/blob/7a6b95d17bde142343a81adcd7cc27bd5bbd3be0/src/Dotnet.Watch/Watch/UI/IReporter.cs#L170-L171) still indexes the dictionary directly. `Microsoft.DotNet.HotReload.Watch.Aspire` 10.0.4xx doesn't have the browser tools path and isn't affected.

### Repro

1. Create a `Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Web` project (net10.0) and select SDK 11.0.100.
2. Run it under the Aspire watch server with `Configuration=Release` and `Optimize=false` in the server's environment. That's how Aspire builds watched services in Release, without the workaround below.
3. The resource launch fails with the message above.

Plain `dotnet watch` probably fails the same way, because it uses the same logger. I haven't verified that.

### Suggested fix

Do either or both of the following:

- mirror `LogEvents.BrowserToolsNotSupportedByProjectSettings` (and any other `LogEvents` entries that aren't mirrored yet) into `MessageDescriptor`;
- make `GetDescriptor` tolerant: `s_descriptors.GetValueOrDefault(id)`, falling back to level-based emoji selection.

### Workaround

The build host can set `EnableHotReloadInRuntimeConfigDevFile=true` for non-Debug builds, which the SDK documents as the switch for its hot reload build outputs. Projects that disable static web assets or JS modules have no workaround other than not watching them.

Issues.Title: [dotnet test] Coordinate MTP invocation-lifetime handlers across test modules
Issues.Body:
### Agent assessment Self-reported assessment, not an independent review. Assessed revision: `2b26a947128aa570fa2b284d68c158b6b8232173` | Dimension | Assessment | Rationale | |---|---|---| | Change confidence | 8/10 | ↑ 33/33 composed E2E scenarios pass against this head with packed TestFx bits, including mixed old/new MTP binaries.
↑ 161/161 focused dotnet.Tests (coordinator, owner selector, IPC, serializers, action queue, launch, protocol version) pass at this head.
↓ Composed runs used TestFx packages from microsoft/testfx@a04da10b, not the current microsoft/testfx#12633 head.
↓ The `GivenDotnetTestBuildsAndRunsTests` rerun at this head was not completed; those rows last passed at 694c8303653.
↓ CI has not run yet. | > [!NOTE] > Draft companion PR for microsoft/testfx#12633. It depends on Microsoft.Testing.Platform protocol 1.5.0, which has not shipped yet. Do not merge until the TestFx side ships and the contract is final. ## Summary This PR adds the `dotnet test` (Microsoft.Testing.Platform mode) consumer side of invocation-lifetime coordination. The design is described in [microsoft/testfx RFC 024 §8.1–8.4](https://github.com/microsoft/testfx/blob/main/docs/RFCs/024-Invocation-Lifecycle-Hooks.md), which remains the decision record. When several test modules register the same invocation-lifetime handlers, the SDK picks one owner module. Setup and cleanup then run once for the whole `dotnet test` invocation instead of once per module: - **Owner selection.** `InvocationLifetimeOwnerSelector` uses the MSBuild handler metadata, or picks an owner automatically. - **Handshake.** The owner advertises its enabled handler UIDs in handshake property 23 (a JSON array). The SDK replies with property 24, `InvocationLifetimeCoordinationAccepted=true`. The owner starts setup only after it receives that explicit acceptance. - **Sibling launch.** Siblings start only after `InvocationSetupCompleted` (serializer 16). They receive the coordinated handler UIDs and their setup outputs. - **Cleanup.** After every module finishes (`ModuleTestsCompleted`, serializer 17), the SDK sends `RunInvocationCleanup` (server control kind 3, with fields AggregateExitCode and IsCanceled). It sends it only to the owner's control connection. The owner then reports `InvocationCleanupCompleted` (serializer 18). - **Terminal slot.** The detached owner keeps its parallelism and terminal slot until the process exits. - **Policies.** Test policies (minimum expected tests, zero tests, ignore exit codes) are applied before cleanup runs. Cleanup therefore receives the same aggregate exit code that `dotnet test` returns. ### Compatibility and fallback In the following cases the SDK uses Phase 1 behavior: each module runs its own handlers, and the SDK prints at most one concise warning before any module starts. - Protocol below 1.5, or no named-pipe control capability. - Missing handler metadata, a UID mismatch, or a sibling that does not support coordination. - Discovery (`--list-tests`). MTP never runs invocation handlers during discovery, so the SDK prints no warning here. - `--no-build`. The SDK cannot prove that the runnable binaries are current. - `--no-dependencies` or `BuildProjectReferences=false`. Project-reference outputs might be stale. If a failure happens after setup might have started, the SDK fails without launching siblings. When no module registers handlers, behavior is unchanged. ### User-visible changes - New localized warnings explain why coordination fell back to Phase 1 (`--no-build`, `--no-dependencies`, unsupported sibling). - The SDK exports the role and coordinated-UID environment variables to modules only in coordinated runs. ## Validation Final head: `2b26a947128aa570fa2b284d68c158b6b8232173`. The redist `dotnet.dll` SHA256 is `ED55808332CC24080679B0B983BD292010F139E3964F6262943A6382B26205CC`. ### Focused tests The focused tests ran with `scripts\RunTests.cs` against `test\dotnet.Tests` at this head, using the filter `InvocationLifetime|TestApplicationActionQueueTests|TestApplicationLaunchTests|IPCTests|ServerControlMessageSerializerTests|TestApplicationProtocolVersionTests`. Result: **161/161 passed**. At `694c8303653`, the earlier focused run that also covered `GivenDotnetTestBuildsAndRunsTests` passed 280/280. That run included the real-SDK `--no-dependencies` rows. ### Composed end-to-end tests The composed tests used the redist built from this head and locally packed TestFx `3.0.0-dev`. Each case ran `dotnet test --solution E2E.slnx` plus the listed arguments. The environment set: - `DOTNET_ROOT` - `DOTNET_CLI_HOME` - `NUGET_PACKAGES` - `DOTNET_ADD_GLOBAL_TOOLS_TO_PATH=0` - `DOTNET_CLI_UI_LANGUAGE=en` - `DOTNET_CLI_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT=1` A pass in Phase 2 means 2 setup and 2 cleanup callbacks, all in the Owner, with cleanup order B then A. A pass in Phase 1 means 6 setup and 6 cleanup callbacks, 2 per module. Issues.Title: Remove the legacy Aspire workload deprecation check from the .NET SDK
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Remove `_CheckForAspireWorkloadDeprecation` and its import from the .NET SDK. The workload-based Aspire project model dates back more than three years; we should retire this migration check rather than require modern, SDK-free AppHosts to keep supplying an obsolete SDK-version marker.

## Current behavior

[`Microsoft.NET.AspireWorkloadDeprecation.targets`](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/blob/main/src/Tasks/Microsoft.NET.Build.Tasks/targets/Microsoft.NET.AspireWorkloadDeprecation.targets) runs before `PrepareForBuild`. If `IsAspireHost` is `true` and `AspireHostingSDKVersion` is empty or below `9.0.0`, it raises `AspireWorkloadIsDeprecated`.

Current Aspire AppHosts use `Microsoft.NET.Sdk` plus the `Aspire.Hosting.AppHost` package, without `Aspire.AppHost.Sdk`. To avoid this error, the package sets `AspireHostingSDKVersion` to its own package version even though no Aspire SDK is being used.

Related Aspire changes: https://github.com/microsoft/aspire/pull/22454 and the release/17.0 backport https://github.com/microsoft/aspire/pull/22636. The backport makes this workaround available earlier during project evaluation; it does not eliminate the underlying SDK dependency.

## Requested change and follow-up

- Remove the SDK target and its import so package-based AppHosts do not need an Aspire SDK-version property merely to pass this check.
- Once the removal is available in the .NET SDKs supported by Aspire, return to `Aspire.Hosting.AppHost` and remove the synthetic `AspireHostingSDKVersion` defaults from its package `.props` and `.targets`. These assignments should be treated as a temporary compatibility workaround, not a long-term contract.
- Audit and migrate remaining Aspire tooling consumers before removing those defaults. Keep `_AspireAppHostPackageVersion` where it represents the actual package version, including CLI version pinning.
- Link this issue from a comment above the property group in `Aspire.Hosting.AppHost.in.props` so the reason for the workaround and its removal condition are clear.

Removing the check in future SDKs alone is not sufficient to delete the package workaround while Aspire still supports SDK versions that contain the check.

Unknown.

That would point to queue or machine infrastructure rather than repository code. This is not confirmed: the Helix console and the ADO timeline were not retrievable from the triage host, so it is unknown whether the test process hung, crashed, or never started.

Issues.Title: [Known Build Error] SdkAppHostLayoutTests.AppHostsAreGeneratedPerHostAndTypeLibraryIsIndependent intermittently misses MSBuild apphost regeneration
Issues.Body:
## Build Information
Build: https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1699020
Build error leg or test failing: `sdk-tasks.Tests.dll.3` (Windows x64 - windows.amd64.vs2026.pre.scout.open), `Microsoft.CoreSdkTasks.Tests.SdkAppHostLayoutTests.AppHostsAreGeneratedPerHostAndTypeLibraryIsIndependent`
Pull request: dotnet/sdk#57346 (release/11.0.2xx → main merge; neither the test nor `GenerateLayout.targets` is changed relative to `main`)

## Error Message

```
Expected string not to be "MSBuild.dll|resources=updated MSBuild.dll|24aff22ab5904c1cbe942493ecf97ba8".
   at Microsoft.CoreSdkTasks.Tests.SdkAppHostLayoutTests.AppHostsAreGeneratedPerHostAndTypeLibraryIsIndependent() in /_/test/sdk-tasks.Tests/SdkAppHostLayoutTests.cs:line 126
```

Build Analysis reports a 0.72% historical failure rate for this test. It passed 10/10 repeated local runs on Windows at the same commit.

## Likely cause (inference)

The test, added in dotnet/sdk#56764, rewrites an input file (`File.WriteAllText`) immediately after a build and expects the next build to regenerate every apphost. `_GenerateMSBuildAppHost` in `src/Layout/redist/targets/GenerateLayout.targets` relies only on MSBuild `Inputs`/`Outputs` timestamps. NTFS last-write times advance at clock-tick granularity, so an input written within the same tick as the previous output is not newer, and the target is skipped. Only the MSBuild host failed. It is generated last, so its output timestamp is closest to the subsequent input write, which is consistent with this explanation.

Possible fix: in the test, advance rewritten input timestamps explicitly, or set prior outputs to an older timestamp, before each rebuild that expects regeneration.

```json
{
  "ErrorMessage": "SdkAppHostLayoutTests.AppHostsAreGeneratedPerHostAndTypeLibraryIsIndependent",

  "BuildRetry": false,
  "ExcludeConsoleLog": false
}
```

Issues.Title: Expose the generated multi-platform container index digest
Issues.Body:
Multi-platform container publishes expose the serialized image index but no digest output. Build integrations that need an immutable reference for signing, attestations, or deployment must hash the JSON themselves or query the registry.

Expose `GeneratedImageIndexDigest` on `CreateImageIndex` and as an MSBuild property, computed from the same serialized bytes as `GeneratedImageIndex`. It identifies the final OCI image index or Docker manifest list, including its annotations. For archives, it identifies the referenced index blob rather than the root `index.json` wrapper or the tar file. Like the existing generated-content outputs, it does not confirm a successful push.

Regression coverage independently hashes the archived index and the actual registry PUT bodies for two tags, with multithreaded MSBuild enabled and disabled. It also checks empty outputs before generation and preserves the generated identity when publishing subsequently fails.

Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/sdk-container-builds/issues/653

Issues.Title: Make test run timeout checks deterministic
Issues.Body:
### Agent assessment Self-reported assessment, not an independent review. Assessed revision: `9b3a0fe0144561baf25062cda115ffb51b3a69a7` | Dimension | Assessment | Rationale | |---|---|---| | Change confidence | 8.5/10 | ↑ Manual-clock checks cover startup, the exact deadline, cancellation, and additional applications.
↑ Windows Debug policy and real-timer command tests passed five times.
↓ Historical CI conditions were not reproduced. | | Diagnosis confidence | 8/10 | ↑ The affected test waited five seconds for a real timer, making the assertion dependent on callback scheduling.
↓ Available CI evidence cannot establish whether the callback was delayed or cancellation was never published. | | Evidence fit | 7/10 | ↑ The recorded failure was a timeout at the affected cancellation wait.
↓ No retained diagnostics establish the underlying cause. | The timeout policy test can fail while waiting for a real timer under CI scheduling delays. Use the existing manual clock to verify that the timeout starts with the first application, fires at the deadline, and is not reset by additional applications. Real-timer concurrency and command-level timeout coverage remain in place. The [historical CI result](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1690099&view=ms.vss-test-web.build-test-results-tab&runId=47177742&resultId=103809&paneView=debug) does not identify why cancellation was not observed, so this change does not establish a product-level root cause. **Validation:** Windows Debug redist build; eight policy tests and the real-timer command-level timeout test passed in five runs (45/45). Relates to #57252

Issues.Title: Add scheduled poll fallback to PR labeler
Issues.Body:
GitHub blocks `pull_request_target` by default in public repos from December 2 ([changelog](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-02-pull_request_target-blocked-by-default-december-2/)). This adds a scheduled fallback to preserve automatic `Area-` labeling.

- Poll every 5 minutes for open PRs without an `Area-` label.
- Manual dispatch without PR numbers processes all open unlabeled PRs.
- Scheduled/manual runs fail on cache misses or prediction errors. Quiet mode is disabled so the pinned v2.0.0 action enforces cache-miss failures.
- `pull_request_target` remains unchanged.

The first scheduled run will try the roughly 147 open PRs without an `Area-` label. Some may remain unlabeled at the 0.40 threshold.

Issues.Title: Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-118740 - Aspire Security Feature Bypass Vulnerability
Issues.Body: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in Aspire. This advisory provides guidance on updating affected applications and components. Aspire Dashboard's unauthenticated NotFound route can permit telemetry deletion in both standalone and AppHost-hosted deployments. In standalone deployments using browser-token authentication, it can also expose the browser token. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/microsoft/aspire/issues/22148 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** Critical - **Score:** 9.1 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N` - **Weakness:** CWE-862 ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Any supported OS - **Architectures:** x64, Arm64 ## Affected Packages ### Standalone Aspire Dashboard Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- Aspire Dashboard | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 Both 13.6.3 and 13.6.4 contain the unauthenticated NotFound route. ### Aspire Dashboard SDK packages Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.linux-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.linux-x64) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.linux-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.linux-arm64) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.linux-musl-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.linux-musl-x64) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.osx-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.osx-x64) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.osx-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.osx-arm64) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.win-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.win-x64) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.win-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.win-arm64) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? Aspire Dashboard releases through 13.6.4 are affected, whether deployed independently or launched by an Aspire AppHost. For an AppHost using Dashboard SDK packages, check the resolved Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk package versions against the affected ranges above. If the AppHost selects a CLI-bundled Dashboard or a custom Dashboard path, check the version of that Dashboard instead. Aspire ships independently of .NET; installing a .NET runtime or SDK update does not replace the Dashboard. ### How do I fix the issue? Update Aspire Dashboard to version 13.6.5 or later. Neither 13.6.3 nor 13.6.4 is a fixed upgrade target. For container deployments, explicitly set the Dashboard image to `mcr.microsoft.com/aspire/dashboard:13.6.5` and recreate or redeploy the container. Replace older version tags and nightly image references, including those in generated Docker Compose or Kubernetes manifests, with this fixed stable image. Updating AppHost package references alone does not replace an image reference in an existing deployment manifest. For an AppHost using Dashboard SDK packages, update any explicit Aspire.Hosting.AppHost version, including a central package version, to 13.6.5 or later. If that reference is supplied implicitly by Aspire.AppHost.Sdk, update the SDK reference to 13.6.5 or later instead. Restore and rebuild the AppHost, verify that its resolved Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk packages are 13.6.5 or later, and restart the AppHost to run the updated Dashboard. If your AppHost selects a CLI-bundled Dashboard or a custom Dashboard path, update the Dashboard in that selected bundle or location to 13.6.5 or later and restart the AppHost. Updating AppHost package references alone does not replace that Dashboard. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Further information can be found in the MSRC [Report an Issue FAQ](https://www.microsoft.com/msrc/faqs-report-an-issue). Security reports made through MSRC may qualify for the Microsoft .NET Bounty. Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue in the Aspire repository at https://github.com/microsoft/aspire. The Announcements repo (https://github.com/dotnet/Announcements) will contain this bulletin as an issue and will include a link to a discussion issue. You can ask questions in the linked discussion issue. ### Disclaimer The information provided in this advisory is provided "as is" without warranty of any kind. Microsoft disclaims all warranties, either express or implied, including the warranties of merchantability and fitness for a particular purpose. In no event shall Microsoft Corporation or its suppliers be liable for any damages whatsoever including direct, indirect, incidental, consequential, loss of business profits or special damages, even if Microsoft Corporation or its suppliers have been advised of the possibility of such damages. Some states do not allow the exclusion or limitation of liability for consequential or incidental damages so the foregoing limitation may not apply. ### External Links [CVE-2026-118740](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-118740) ### Acknowledgements - Weeraphat Srisutham ### Revisions V1.0 (November 10, 2026): Advisory published.

Issues.Title: Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-118741 | ASP.NET Core Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability
Issues.Body: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in ASP.NET Core. This advisory provides guidance on updating affected applications and components. ASP.NET Core Identity scaffolding templates use the request-supplied email instead of the account's stored email for password-reset and confirmation messages. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/Scaffolding/issues/3959 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 8.1 (base score) - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H/E:U/RL:O/RC:C` - **Weakness:** CWE-640 ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Any supported OS - **Architectures:** All ## Affected Packages Updating scaffolding packages/tools does not repair previously generated application code. Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc contains the affected templates. Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design is a parent package that brings in the MVC generator through a minimum-version dependency. For Design, applicability depends on the resolved MVC generator: a project that independently resolves a fixed MVC version does not become vulnerable merely because it retains an older Design reference. ### 8.0 - standalone packages Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc) | >= 8.0.0, <= 8.0.23 | 8.0.24 [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design) | >= 8.0.0, <= 8.0.23 | 8.0.24 ### 9.0 - standalone packages Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc) | >= 9.0.0, <= 9.0.12 | 9.0.13 [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design) | >= 9.0.0, <= 9.0.12 | 9.0.13 ### 10.0 - standalone packages Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc) | >= 10.0.0, <= 10.0.2 | 10.0.3 [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design) | >= 10.0.0, <= 10.0.2 | 10.0.3 ### Additional known affected scaffolding prereleases These are exact known affected versions, not continuous prerelease intervals. Version 20.3.0 supports .NET 8, 9, 10 and 11. Install it as a .NET tool, not as a project package reference. The MVC and Design project packages use the separate fixed versions listed above; 20.3.0 is not a version of those packages. ### Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold 20.x Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold) | >= 20.0.0-preview.1.26156.3, <= 20.1.0 | 20.3.0 The 20.x tool contains the vulnerable Identity and Blazor templates for .NET 8.0 through 11.0. ### Affected legacy prereleases The following exact versions also contain affected templates: - [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc) and [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design): `11.0.0-preview.1.26156.3` and `11.0.0-preview.1.26230.3`. - [Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold-aspnet](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold-aspnet): `10.0.0-rc.1.25458.5` and `10.0.0-rc.1.25468.1`. Apply the generated-code repair below to applications created with these versions. For new scaffolding, use the Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold 20.3.0 tool, which supports .NET 8 through 11. Migrating to that tool is not an update to an MVC or Design project package reference and does not repair previously generated code. ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? Check both the installed scaffolding package/tool version and the code it generated. Applications generated with an affected template remain affected after the tool is updated unless their handlers are corrected. The `dotnet-aspnet-codegenerator` command loads generators from the application's dependencies. Check the project's Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design and Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc references against the versions above; updating only the command-line tool does not replace those project dependencies. For applications created with `dotnet new`, check the selected SDK with `dotnet --version` in the working directory. Use `dotnet new list` to identify available templates and `dotnet new uninstall` without arguments to list separately installed template packages. Web ProjectTemplates can be bundled with an SDK or installed separately; a project package reference alone does not identify which template generated the application. ### How do I fix the issue? Update affected scaffolding packages/tools and project dependencies to the patched versions above before generating additional code. Updating scaffolding packages/tools does not repair previously generated applications. Change generated ForgotPassword and ResendEmailConfirmation handlers, including Blazor equivalents, to send only to the stored email returned for the located user; reject missing stored addresses, rebuild and redeploy affected apps. For an existing global Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold installation, update the tool: ```shell dotnet tool update --global Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold --version 20.3.0 ``` For Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold-aspnet installations, uninstall the old tool and install its replacement: ```shell dotnet tool uninstall --global Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold-aspnet dotnet tool install --global Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold --version 20.3.0 ``` For a new installation, use the install command alone. For local tools, use `--local` instead of `--global` and run the commands from the directory containing the tool manifest. Visual Studio installs and uses the updated scaffolding tool automatically; command-line installations must be updated separately. Visual Studio 17.14 uses the legacy CodeGeneration packages listed above; keep Visual Studio updated and check independently maintained project dependencies. For SDK-bundled templates, install and select an updated SDK that includes the corrected ProjectTemplates version; check `global.json` if an older SDK remains selected. Update separately installed template packs independently. Updating the SDK does not necessarily replace a separately installed template pack. For the affected legacy prereleases, correct the generated handlers before using or deploying the generated application. #### Manual repair for generated Identity handlers This repair also applies to applications generated with the affected 11.0 scaffolding packages and Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold-aspnet 10.0 RC versions above; it does not require migrating to a different scaffolding tool. In the generated `ForgotPassword` and `ResendEmailConfirmation` handlers, retain the existing user lookup, missing-user responses, password-reset confirmation checks, token generation and callback-URL encoding. After those user checks, retrieve the email from the located account before sending: ```csharp var storedEmail = await UserManager.GetEmailAsync(user); if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(storedEmail)) { throw new InvalidOperationException("Users must have an email."); } ``` In Razor Pages handlers, use `_userManager` instead of `UserManager`. Replace only the recipient argument `Input.Email` with `storedEmail` in `_emailSender.SendEmailAsync`, `EmailSender.SendPasswordResetLinkAsync` and `EmailSender.SendConfirmationLinkAsync`, as applicable. Keep `Input.Email` for the account lookup; do not use it as the message recipient. Apply the change to both handlers, including their Blazor equivalents, then rebuild and redeploy. Reapply the repair if affected templates generate the handlers again. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). This advisory provides guidance on updating affected applications and components. know if I am affected? Check the deployed runtime and application package versions against the affected ranges above. Self-contained applications include their own runtime; updating a machine-wide runtime does not replace it. ### How do I fix the issue? Install the applicable runtime or update each independently referenced package to the fixed version above. After updating standalone packages, rebuild and redeploy affected applications, including framework-dependent applications; restarting alone does not replace app-local packages. Restart applications. Rebuild and redeploy self-contained applications; updating a machine-wide runtime does not replace their embedded runtime. An SDK update alone does not update an application's standalone package references. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Issues.Body: > **Announcement consolidated:** See the [November 2026 ASP.NET Core security announcement](https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/504) and [shared feedback thread](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/discussions/70467). This original CVE post is retained for existing links. Closing it does not withdraw the advisory or its remediation guidance. ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in ASP.NET Core. This advisory provides guidance on updating affected applications and components. SignalR Redis scale-out can mishandle case-mismatched group removal and leave subscriptions in a state that permits persistent resource amplification and denial of service. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/discussions/70467 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 7.5 (base score) - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H/E:U/RL:O/RC:C` - **Weakness:** CWE-401 ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Windows, Linux, macOS - **Architectures:** All ## Affected Packages The tables list affected version ranges and fixed package versions. Issues.Body: > **Announcement consolidated:** See the [November 2026 .NET Runtime security announcement](https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/498) and [shared feedback thread](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/137280). This original CVE post is retained for existing links. Closing it does not withdraw the advisory or its remediation guidance. ## Executive Summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in .NET. This advisory provides guidance on updating affected applications and components. Crafted PDB line metadata can exceed the caller-provided buffer and cause a heap out-of-bounds write. ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 8.8 (base score) - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H/E:U/RL:O/RC:C` - **Weakness:** CWE-122 ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Windows - **Architectures:** x86, x64, Arm64 ## Affected Packages On Windows x86, x64, and Arm64, Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native versions earlier than 18.9.1-beta1.26515.1 are affected when reading crafted native PDBs. ### .NET on Windows Product | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- .NET 8.0 installed on Windows | >= 8.0.0, < 8.0.34 | 8.0.34 .NET 9.0 installed on Windows | >= 9.0.0, < 9.0.23 | 9.0.23 .NET 10.0 installed on Windows | >= 10.0.0, < 10.0.15 | 10.0.15 .NET 11.0 installed on Windows | >= 11.0.0-preview.1, < 11.0.0 | 11.0.0 ### Windows self-contained runtime packs These runtime packs deliver the .NET runtime for Windows self-contained applications. Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.win-x86](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.win-x86) | >= 8.0.0, < 8.0.34 | 8.0.34 [Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.win-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.win-x64) | >= 8.0.0, < 8.0.34 | 8.0.34 [Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.win-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.win-arm64) | >= 8.0.0, < 8.0.34 | 8.0.34 [Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.win-x86](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.win-x86) | >= 9.0.0, < 9.0.23 | 9.0.23 [Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.win-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.win-x64) | >= 9.0.0, < 9.0.23 | 9.0.23 [Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.win-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.win-arm64) | >= 9.0.0, < 9.0.23 | 9.0.23 [Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.win-x86](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.win-x86) | >= 10.0.0, < 10.0.15 | 10.0.15 [Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.win-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.win-x64) | >= 10.0.0, < 10.0.15 | 10.0.15 [Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.win-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.win-arm64) | >= 10.0.0, < 10.0.15 | 10.0.15 [Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.win-x86](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.win-x86) | >= 11.0.0-preview.1, < 11.0.0 | 11.0.0 [Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.win-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.win-x64) | >= 11.0.0-preview.1, < 11.0.0 | 11.0.0 [Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.win-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.win-arm64) | >= 11.0.0-preview.1, < 11.0.0 | 11.0.0 ### Windows SDK distributions These Windows SDK distributions are affected through their bundled .NET runtime. Product | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- .NET SDK 8.0.1xx | >= 8.0.100-0, < 8.0.134 | 8.0.134 .NET SDK 8.0.4xx | >= 8.0.400-0, < 8.0.428 | 8.0.428 .NET SDK 9.0.1xx | >= 9.0.100-0, < 9.0.124 | 9.0.124 .NET SDK 9.0.3xx | >= 9.0.300-0, < 9.0.321 | 9.0.321 .NET SDK 10.0.1xx | >= 10.0.100-0, < 10.0.115 | 10.0.115 .NET SDK 10.0.4xx | >= 10.0.400-0, < 10.0.404 | 10.0.404 .NET SDK 11.0.1xx | >= 11.0.100-preview.1, < 11.0.100 | 11.0.100 ### Windows SDK updates Update each installed SDK feature band to the following version or later: - .NET SDK 8.0.1xx: 8.0.134 - .NET SDK 8.0.4xx: 8.0.428 - .NET SDK 9.0.1xx: 9.0.124 - .NET SDK 9.0.3xx: 9.0.321 - .NET SDK 10.0.1xx: 10.0.115 - .NET SDK 10.0.4xx: 10.0.404 - .NET SDK 11.0.1xx: 11.0.100 ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? Applications using Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native versions earlier than 18.9.1-beta1.26515.1 on Windows x86, x64, and Arm64 to read crafted native PDBs are exposed. See [affected packages](#affected-packages) for the affected .NET products on Windows. ### How do I fix the issue? Update affected .NET installations and each installed SDK feature band to the versions listed above or later. If an SDK was installed through Visual Studio, update Visual Studio as well. Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native is delivered through .NET Core rather than as a standalone customer NuGet update. For applications that deploy their own affected .NET runtime, including self-contained applications, update the runtime used to build the application, rebuild, and redeploy. Updating a machine-wide runtime does not replace an application's embedded runtime. Restart processes that have loaded the affected native reader. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/137280 ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Further information can be found in the MSRC [Report an Issue FAQ](https://www.microsoft.com/msrc/faqs-report-an-issue). Security reports made through MSRC may qualify for the Microsoft .NET Bounty. Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue on GitHub in the .NET GitHub organization. Issues.Title: Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-120778 - Aspire Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability
Issues.Body: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in the Aspire CLI. This advisory provides guidance on updating affected applications and components. An insecure temporary directory used by Aspire CLI-generated builds can allow a local attacker to influence MSBuild response-file discovery and execute code with the privileges of the developer running the CLI. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/microsoft/aspire/issues/22101 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 7.3 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H` - **Weakness:** CWE-379 (Creation of Temporary File in Directory with Insecure Permissions) - **MSRC severity:** Important ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Linux, macOS - **Architectures:** x64, Arm64 ## Affected Packages ### Standalone Aspire CLI Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Aspire.Cli](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Cli) | >= 13.2.0, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Cli.linux-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Cli.linux-x64) | >= 13.3.0, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Cli.linux-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Cli.linux-arm64) | >= 13.3.0, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Cli.linux-musl-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Cli.linux-musl-x64) | >= 13.3.0, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Cli.osx-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Cli.osx-x64) | >= 13.3.0, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Cli.osx-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Cli.osx-arm64) | >= 13.3.0, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 ### Aspire CLI npm packages Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [@microsoft/aspire-cli](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@microsoft/aspire-cli) | >= 13.4.2, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [@microsoft/aspire-cli-linux-x64](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@microsoft/aspire-cli-linux-x64) | >= 13.4.2, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [@microsoft/aspire-cli-linux-arm64](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@microsoft/aspire-cli-linux-arm64) | >= 13.4.2, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [@microsoft/aspire-cli-linux-musl-x64](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@microsoft/aspire-cli-linux-musl-x64) | >= 13.4.2, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [@microsoft/aspire-cli-osx-x64](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@microsoft/aspire-cli-osx-x64) | >= 13.4.2, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [@microsoft/aspire-cli-osx-arm64](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@microsoft/aspire-cli-osx-arm64) | >= 13.4.2, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 The affected scenario concerns CLI-generated server and integration builds on non-Windows systems when a local attacker can influence automatic MSBuild response-file discovery through an attacker-writable directory. This includes builds started by `aspire sdk generate`, `aspire sdk dump`, and `aspire sdk export`. ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? The reported scenario involves a local attacker influencing a generated build through a shared temporary-directory ancestor while another user invokes the Aspire CLI. Versions 13.2.0 through 13.6.4 are affected. Aspire ships independently of .NET. Installing a .NET runtime or SDK update does not establish that the affected Aspire CLI has been updated. ### How do I fix the issue? Update the Aspire CLI to version 13.6.5 or later. If installed as a .NET tool, update the Aspire.Cli package. If installed using npm, update @microsoft/aspire-cli to version 13.6.5 or later; its platform-specific dependency must also resolve to version 13.6.5 or later. Otherwise update the CLI through its installation method. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Further information can be found in the MSRC [Report an Issue FAQ](https://www.microsoft.com/msrc/faqs-report-an-issue). Security reports made through MSRC may qualify for the Microsoft .NET Bounty. Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue in the [Aspire repository](https://github.com/microsoft/aspire). ### Disclaimer The information provided in this advisory is provided "as is" without warranty of any kind. **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 7.3 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:R/S:C/C:H/I:L/A:L` - **Weakness:** CWE-532 (Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File) - **MSRC severity:** Important - **Impact:** Information Disclosure ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Linux, macOS - **Architectures:** x64, Arm64 ## Affected Packages ### Standalone Aspire CLI Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- Aspire CLI ([Aspire.Cli](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Cli)) | >= 13.2.0, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Cli.linux-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Cli.linux-x64) | >= 13.3.0, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Cli.linux-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Cli.linux-arm64) | >= 13.3.0, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Cli.linux-musl-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Cli.linux-musl-x64) | >= 13.3.0, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Cli.osx-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Cli.osx-x64) | >= 13.3.0, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Cli.osx-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Cli.osx-arm64) | >= 13.3.0, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 ### Aspire CLI npm packages Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [@microsoft/aspire-cli](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@microsoft/aspire-cli) | >= 13.4.2, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [@microsoft/aspire-cli-linux-x64](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@microsoft/aspire-cli-linux-x64) | >= 13.4.2, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [@microsoft/aspire-cli-linux-arm64](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@microsoft/aspire-cli-linux-arm64) | >= 13.4.2, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [@microsoft/aspire-cli-linux-musl-x64](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@microsoft/aspire-cli-linux-musl-x64) | >= 13.4.2, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [@microsoft/aspire-cli-osx-x64](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@microsoft/aspire-cli-osx-x64) | >= 13.4.2, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [@microsoft/aspire-cli-osx-arm64](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@microsoft/aspire-cli-osx-arm64) | >= 13.4.2, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 The affected component is the Aspire CLI's deprecated MCP configuration scanner, which ships in the CLI packages listed above. Its temporary-file diagnostics can include configuration content and use a fixed path in a shared temporary directory. ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? The reported scenario involves running Aspire CLI agent or MCP initialization commands on a non-Windows system with a temporary directory shared by multiple users. Versions 13.2.0 through 13.6.4 are affected. Aspire ships independently of .NET. Installing a .NET runtime or SDK update does not establish that the affected Aspire CLI has been updated. ### How do I fix the issue? Update the Aspire CLI to version 13.6.5 or later. If installed as a .NET tool, update the Aspire.Cli package. If installed using npm, update @microsoft/aspire-cli to version 13.6.5 or later; its platform-specific dependency must also resolve to version 13.6.5 or later. Otherwise update the CLI through its installation method. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue in the [Aspire repository](https://github.com/microsoft/aspire). ### Disclaimer The information provided in this advisory is provided "as is" without warranty of any kind. Issues.Title: Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-120006 - Aspire Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability
Issues.Body: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in Aspire. This advisory provides guidance on updating affected applications and components. Disclosure of an Aspire Dashboard authentication cookie to a linked service can allow an attacker-controlled container to replay the authenticated session and execute code as the host developer. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/microsoft/aspire/issues/22092 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 7.5 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:H/PR:L/UI:R/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H` - **Weakness:** CWE-201 (Insertion of Sensitive Information Into Sent Data) ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** macOS - **Architectures:** x64, Arm64 ## Affected Packages ### Standalone Aspire Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Aspire.Hosting.AppHost](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Hosting.AppHost) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Hosting](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Hosting) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 The affected scenario involves a Dashboard-authenticated AppHost workflow with an attacker-controlled container and a linked HTTPS YARP gateway. The affected hosting code is in `Aspire.Hosting`, a dependency of `Aspire.Hosting.AppHost`. `Aspire.AppHost.Sdk` supplies the AppHost package implicitly unless the project overrides the default references. ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? The reported scenario involves a developer starting an Aspire AppHost, authenticating to its Dashboard, and following a resource link that routes to an attacker-controlled container. All released versions through 13.6.4 are affected. Aspire ships independently of .NET. Installing a .NET runtime or SDK update does not establish that the affected Aspire components have been updated. ### How do I fix the issue? Update the AppHost project's `Aspire.Hosting.AppHost` package reference to version 13.6.5 or later. If the project obtains this package implicitly through `Aspire.AppHost.Sdk`, update that SDK reference to version 13.6.5 or later. Explicit package references or central version pins must also resolve `Aspire.Hosting` to version 13.6.5 or later. Restore dependencies, rebuild, and restart the AppHost after updating. Updating only the .NET runtime, .NET SDK, Aspire CLI, or standalone Dashboard does not replace the AppHost project's hosting dependencies. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Further information can be found in the MSRC [Report an Issue FAQ](https://www.microsoft.com/msrc/faqs-report-an-issue). Security reports made through MSRC may qualify for the Microsoft .NET Bounty. Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue in the [Aspire repository](https://github.com/microsoft/aspire). ### Disclaimer The information provided in this advisory is provided "as is" without warranty of any kind. Microsoft disclaims all warranties, either express or implied, including the warranties of merchantability and fitness for a particular purpose. In no event shall Microsoft Corporation or its suppliers be liable for any damages whatsoever including direct, indirect, incidental, consequential, loss of business profits or special damages, even if Microsoft Corporation or its suppliers have been advised of the possibility of such damages. Some states do not allow the exclusion or limitation of liability for consequential or incidental damages so the foregoing limitation may not apply. ### External Links [CVE-2026-120006](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-120006) ### Acknowledgements - samthewhitehat ### Revisions V1.0 (November 10, 2026): Advisory published.

Issues.Title: Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-114155 - .NET Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability
Issues.Body: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in the .NET SDK's dotnet-watch component. This advisory provides guidance on updating affected SDK installations. A local attacker who can replace or modify a temporary solution file used by dotnet-watch can alter a subsequent build. The fix stores generated solution files in a private temporary directory and keeps each file open with read-only sharing while the build uses it. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/issues/57040 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 7.5 (base score) - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:H/PR:L/UI:R/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H/E:U/RL:O/RC:C` - **Weakness:** CWE-367 - **MSRC severity:** Important - **Impact:** Elevation of Privilege ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Linux, macOS. - **Architectures:** Linux: Arm, Arm64, x64; macOS: Arm64, x64 Windows is outside this advisory's affected scope when its temporary directory is private to the current user, as assumed by the implementation. Shared or insecurely configured Windows temporary directories are not covered by that assumption. ## Affected Packages The .NET SDK includes dotnet-watch and the Microsoft.DotNet.HotReload.Watch assembly. Each SDK feature band is a separate servicing line. Update an affected 10.0.3xx installation to the fixed 10.0.4xx SDK listed below. ### .NET SDK 10.0.3xx Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [.NET SDK (dotnet-watch) 10.0.3xx](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/10.0) | >= 10.0.300, <= 10.0.303 | 10.0.404 ### .NET SDK 10.0.4xx Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [.NET SDK (dotnet-watch) 10.0.4xx](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/10.0) | >= 10.0.400, <= 10.0.403 | 10.0.404 ### .NET SDK 11.0.1xx Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [.NET SDK (dotnet-watch) 11.0.1xx](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/11.0) | >= 11.0.100-preview.3.26207.106, <= 11.0.100-rc.3.26522.148 | 11.0.100 ### Separately restored Aspire watch tool Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Microsoft.DotNet.HotReload.Watch.Aspire](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.DotNet.HotReload.Watch.Aspire) | >= 10.0.300, <= 10.0.303 | 10.0.404 [Microsoft.DotNet.HotReload.Watch.Aspire](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.DotNet.HotReload.Watch.Aspire) | >= 10.0.400, <= 10.0.403 | 10.0.404 [Microsoft.DotNet.HotReload.Watch.Aspire](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.DotNet.HotReload.Watch.Aspire) | >= 11.0.100-preview.3.26207.106, <= 11.0.100-rc.3.26522.148 | 11.0.100 This tool has its own copy of the watch implementation. Updating the SDK does not necessarily replace a separately restored tool. ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? Run `dotnet --version` from the directory where you run dotnet-watch to identify the selected SDK. Use `dotnet --info` and `dotnet --list-sdks` to check its installation path, OS, architecture, and other installed SDKs. Check the nearest applicable `global.json`, including its `version` and `rollForward` settings: installing a newer SDK does not necessarily change the SDK selected for a pinned project. See [.NET SDK selection](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/versions/selection). Review use of dotnet-watch against the affected intervals above. Membership in a listed feature band alone does not establish that a specific SDK version is vulnerable. For Aspire or other tooling that separately restores Microsoft.DotNet.HotReload.Watch.Aspire, check the actual restored package version separately from the selected SDK. ### How do I fix the issue? The fixed SDK versions are 10.0.404 and 11.0.100, as applicable. Update each affected SDK installation and restart dotnet-watch. For SDKs installed through Visual Studio, update Visual Studio to a release that includes a fixed SDK. Updating only an application runtime does not replace SDK-bundled tools. Ensure that `global.json` and its SDK roll-forward policy select a fixed SDK, then rerun `dotnet --version` in the working directory to verify the selection. The SDK-bundled watch tool is installed beneath that selected SDK's `DotnetTools/dotnet-watch` directory. If Microsoft.DotNet.HotReload.Watch.Aspire is restored separately, update its package reference or the consuming tool's version configuration to 10.0.404 or 11.0.100, as applicable, restore the tool, and restart the consuming process. An SDK update alone does not update that restored copy. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Further information can be found in the MSRC [Report an Issue FAQ](https://www.microsoft.com/msrc/faqs-report-an-issue). Security reports made through MSRC may qualify for the Microsoft .NET Bounty. Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue on GitHub in the .NET GitHub organization. The main repos are located at https://github.com/dotnet/sdk. The Announcements repo (https://github.com/dotnet/Announcements) will contain this bulletin as an issue and will include a link to a discussion issue. You can ask questions in the linked discussion issue. ### Disclaimer The information provided in this advisory is provided "as is" without warranty of any kind. In no event shall Microsoft Corporation or its suppliers be liable for any damages whatsoever including direct, indirect, incidental, consequential, loss of business profits or special damages, even if Microsoft Corporation or its suppliers have been advised of the possibility of such damages. Some states do not allow the exclusion or limitation of liability for consequential or incidental damages so the foregoing limitation may not apply. ### External Links [CVE-2026-114155](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-114155) ### Acknowledgements - [Ky0toFu](https://x.com/ky0tofu) ### Revisions V1.0 (November 10, 2026): Advisory published.

Original CVE-2026-118746 advisory details (preserved) ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in .NET. This advisory provides guidance on updating affected applications and components. Unix Negotiate authentication can accept a request when required channel-binding information is missing. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/137280 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** Medium - **Score:** 6.8 (base score) - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N/E:U/RL:O/RC:C` - **Weakness:** CWE-636 ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Linux, macOS - **Architectures:** Arm, Arm64, x64 ## Affected Packages The tables list affected .NET 11 runtime package versions and fixed versions. The issue occurs during server-side Negotiate authentication with `PolicyEnforcement.Always` when the client omits the channel-binding token. ### .NET 11.0 - Linux runtime packages Package | Affected version 11.0.0-preview.7.26381.103 reject `PolicyEnforcement.Always` before authentication and are not affected. ### .NET 11.0 - macOS runtime packages Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.osx-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.osx-arm64) | >= 11.0.0-preview.1, < 11.0.0-preview.7.26381.103 | 11.0.0 [Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.osx-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.osx-x64) | >= 11.0.0-preview.1, < 11.0.0-preview.7.26381.103 | 11.0.0 The macOS runtime packages at versions 11.0.0-preview.7.26381.103, 11.0.0-rc.1.26425.128, 11.0.0-rc.2.26504.105, and 11.0.0-rc.3.26522.148 reject `PolicyEnforcement.Always` before authentication and are not affected. ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? Applications using server-side Negotiate authentication with `PolicyEnforcement.Always` are affected when their runtime package version is in the platform-specific ranges above. On Linux, this includes .NET 11 previews 1 through 6 and release candidates 1 through 3. On macOS, this includes .NET 11 previews 1 through 6. Preview 7 is not affected on either platform, and macOS release candidates 1 through 3 are not affected. Self-contained applications include their own runtime; updating a machine-wide runtime does not replace it. ### How do I fix the issue? For affected Linux and macOS .NET 11 prereleases, install .NET 11.0.0 or update each independently referenced runtime package to 11.0.0. Restart applications. Rebuild and redeploy self-contained applications; updating a machine-wide runtime does not replace their embedded runtime. An SDK update alone does not update an application's standalone package references. On macOS, `PolicyEnforcement.Always` remains unsupported and throws `PlatformNotSupportedException`. The update prevents authentication from proceeding without the required protection; it does not add Extended Protection support on macOS. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). The Announcements repo (https://github.com/dotnet/Announcements) will contain this bulletin as an issue and will include a link to a discussion issue. Issues.Title: .NET 11 - Release
Issues.Body:
> This issue is a locked mirror of https://github.com/dotnet/core/discussions/10711. See that thread for discussion.

We are pleased to announce the general availability of .NET 11.

Read about the final release in the [.NET Blog announcement](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/dotnet/announcing-dotnet-11/).

This release includes C# 15, faster developer tools, runtime and library improvements, and new capabilities for web, mobile, desktop, and AI apps. Explore the full release notes below.

## 🛠️ SDK

* [Full Release Notes](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/11.0.0/sdk.md)

## 📱 .NET MAUI

* [Full Release Notes](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/11.0.0/dotnetmaui.md)

## 🎁 Entity Framework Core

* [Full Release Notes](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/11.0.0/efcore.md)

## 📚 Libraries

* [Full Release Notes](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/11.0.0/libraries.md)

## ⏱️ Runtime

* [Full Release Notes](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/11.0.0/runtime.md)

## C# 15

* [Full Release Notes](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/11.0.0/csharp.md)

## F# 11

* [Full Release Notes](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/11.0.0/fsharp.md)

## 🌐 ASP.NET Core & Blazor

* [Full Release Notes](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/11.0.0/aspnetcore.md)

## 🖥️ Windows Forms

* [Full Release Notes](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/11.0.0/winforms.md)

## 🖥️ Windows Presentation Foundation (WPF)

* [Full Release Notes](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/11.0.0/wpf.md)

## 🚀 Get started

To get started with .NET 11, [install the .NET 11 SDK](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/11.0).

If you're on Windows using Visual Studio, use an up-to-date [Visual Studio 2026](https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/vs/) installation that supports .NET 11.

You can also use Visual Studio Code and the [C# Dev Kit](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=ms-dotnettools.csdevkit) extension with .NET 11.

Before upgrading an existing application, review the [breaking changes in .NET 11](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/compatibility/11), update your target frameworks and dependencies, and run your tests.

Celebrate the release of .NET 11 at [.NET Conf 2026](https://dot.net/conf), November 10-13.

## 🔔 Stay up-to-date with .NET 11

You can stay up-to-date with all the features of .NET 11 with:

* [What's new in .NET 11](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/whats-new/dotnet-11/overview)
* [What's new in C# 15](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/csharp/whats-new/csharp-15)
* [What's new in F# 11](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/fsharp/whats-new/fsharp-11)
* [What's new in .NET MAUI](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/maui/whats-new/dotnet-11?view=net-maui-11.0)
* [What's new in ASP.NET Core](https://learn.microsoft.com/aspnet/core/release-notes/aspnetcore-11)
* [What's new in Aspire](https://aspire.dev/whats-new/)
* [What's new in Entity Framework Core](https://learn.microsoft.com/ef/core/what-is-new/ef-core-11.0/whatsnew)
* [What's new in Windows Forms](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/desktop/winforms/whats-new/net110)
* [What's new in WPF](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/desktop/wpf/whats-new/net110)
* [Breaking changes in .NET 11](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/compatibility/11)
* [.NET 11 releases](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/README.md)

Be sure to subscribe to the GitHub Discussions [RSS news feed](https://github.com/dotnet/core/discussions/categories/news.atom) for all release announcements.
